🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever confuses Allah’s Nuzūl with the movements of created beings is only fighting his own conception. The right way is: Allah does what He wills – in a manner that befits Him.

makan-hammad-bin-zayd-nuzul-416.title: 📖 He is in His place
makan-hammad-bin-zayd-nuzul-416.body:
🖋️ **Ḥammād b. Zayd** was asked whether the Ḥadīth of the Nuzūl means that Allah moves from place to place. He said:

***“He is in His place; He draws near to His creation as He wills.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** The statement affirms the Ḥadīth of the Nuzūl and at the same time rejects the created notion of a change of place. The how is not depicted.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Nuzūl is true, but not like the descent of created beings. Ahlus-Sunnah affirm the text and leave the how to Allah.

makan-harb-kirmani-jahmiyyah-417.title: 📖 Jahmiyyah: enemies of Allah
makan-harb-kirmani-jahmiyyah-417.body:
🖋️ **Ḥarb b. Ismāʿīl al-Kirmānī** wrote:

***“The Jahmiyyah are the enemies of Allah. They are those who claim that the Qurʾān is created, that Allah did not speak to Mūsā, that He will not be seen in the Hereafter, that no Makān is known for Allah, and that He is neither upon the Throne nor upon the Kursī. They are Kuffār, so beware of them.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** This statement shows that the denial of **ʿUluww**, of **Kalām Allah**, of the **Ruʾyah**, and of the uncreated Qurʾān was not treated by the early Imāms as a side matter.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Jahmiyyah attacked several foundations of the revelation. Ahlus-Sunnah protect the ʿAqīdah through the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, and the understanding of the Imāms.

makan-ibn-abi-zayd-fawq-arsh-bi-dhatih-4.title: 📖 Allah above the Throne – with His essence
makan-ibn-abi-zayd-fawq-arsh-bi-dhatih-4.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī** said:

***“Allah is above His exalted Throne with His essence, and He is in every place with His knowledge.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** This wording joins two foundations: the **ʿUluww** of Allah above the Throne and the all-encompassing **Maʿiyyah** by knowledge. It does not mean that Allah is everywhere with His essence.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Allah is above the Throne with His essence, and His knowledge encompasses every place. Thereby both **Taʿṭīl** and **Ḥulūl/Ittiḥād** are rejected.

makan-ibn-battah-aala-makan-419.title: 📖 Allah above the ʿArsh – Makān in the sense of exaltation
makan-ibn-battah-aala-makan-419.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Baṭṭah al-ʿUkbarī** explained in substance that our Lord is in the most exalted Makān, in the highest ʿIlliyyīn, above His ʿArsh above His heavens, while His knowledge encompasses the whole creation.

***“He is above His ʿArsh, above His heavens, and His knowledge encompasses everything.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** The term **Makān** is explained here by the context: what is meant is **ʿUluww** and **Fawqiyyah**, not a created space that contains Allah. At the same time Ibn Baṭṭah affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses nearness, distance, the hidden, and the manifest.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Makān must not be understood here in a created sense. What is meant is Allah’s exaltation above the creation, while His knowledge encompasses every place.

makan-ibn-mandah-himmel-tauhid-420.title: 📖 Whoever points to heaven and affirms the Tauḥīd
makan-ibn-mandah-himmel-tauhid-420.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Mandah** set, in substance, as a chapter heading:

***“That which indicates that the one who professes the Tauḥīd by pointing to heaven, thereby meaning that Allah is in heaven and not on the earth, and that Muḥammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, is called a Muʾmin.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** Immediately afterwards Ibn Mandah cites the Ḥadīth of the Jāriyah, in which she answered the question “Where is Allah?” with: “In heaven”, whereupon the Prophet ﷺ said: “Free her, for she is a believer.”

🌙 **Conclusion:** Pointing to heaven is, with Ibn Mandah, a sign of affirming **ʿUluww** and **Tauḥīd**, not a claim that Allah is contained in a created space.

makan-mujmal-al-barrak-421.title: 📖 Makān is a mujmal term
makan-mujmal-al-barrak-421.body:
🖋️ **ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān b. Nāṣir al-Barrāk** explained that the word **Makān** is ambiguous and must therefore be specified.

***“If what is meant by it is a created place that encompasses Allah or contains Him, then Allah is exalted above that. If what is meant is that Allah is above the whole creation, then this is not a false meaning.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** He likewise explained that expressions such as “in His house” are to be understood as **iḍāfat at-tashrīf**, that is, an attribution of honor, not as Allah indwelling the creation.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ambiguous terms are explained. What is false is rejected and what is true is affirmed: Allah is above the creation, but He does not dwell within created beings.

makan-tabari-uluw-makan-422.title: 📖 at-Ṭabarī on ʿUluww and the exalted Makān
makan-tabari-uluw-makan-422.body:
🖋️ **at-Ṭabarī** mentioned, in the tafsīr of **﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ﴾**, a statement that Allah is **above His creation**, by the elevation of His Makān above the Makānāt of His creation.

***“He is above all of His creation, and His creation is beneath Him, just as He has described Himself as being above the Throne.”***

🖋️ Concerning **﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى﴾**, at-Ṭabarī explained in substance:

***“The Most Merciful is above His Throne: He rose and is high.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** at-Ṭabarī does not here affirm a created place that encompasses Allah. Rather, it concerns **ʿUluww**, **Fawqiyyah**, and Allah’s exaltation above all created places.

🌙 **Conclusion:** With at-Ṭabarī, Allah is high above the creation and above the Throne, without being encompassed by created places.

makan-uluw-nuzul-salaf-423.title: 📖 Makān and Nuzūl among the early Imāms
makan-uluw-nuzul-salaf-423.body:
🖋️ **Ḥammād b. Zayd** was asked about the ḥadīth of the **Nuzūl**, whether it means that Allah moves from place to place. He said:

***“He is in His place; He draws near to His creation as He wills.”***

🖋️ **Isḥāq b. Rāhawayh** rejected the objection of whether the ʿArsh becomes empty at the Nuzūl, and explained in substance that Allah is able to descend without the ʿArsh becoming empty.

🖋️ **al-Fuḍayl b. ʿIyāḍ** said:

***“If the Jahmī says: I deny a Lord who departs from His place, then say: I believe in a Lord who does what He wills.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** These early statements affirm the transmitted **Nuzūl** (descent) and at the same time reject a creaturely notion of changing place, movement, or corporeality. The way is: affirm what has come, and leave the how to Allah.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Salaf affirmed the ḥadīth of the Nuzūl without **Tashbīh** and without **Taʿṭīl**. The false frame of thought of the Jahmiyyah is rejected, not the revelation.

malik-adab-vor-wissen-001.title: 📖 Adab before knowledge
malik-adab-vor-wissen-001.body:
🖋️ **Mālik ibn Anas** said to a young man from Quraysh:

> ***“Learn Adab before you learn knowledge.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Knowledge** without **Adab** can make a person proud and harsh. Therefore the path of the learner does not begin only with books, but with ***conduct, humility, and a right dealing with knowledge***.

malik-adab-vor-wissen-396.title: 📖 Adab before the knowledge
malik-adab-vor-wissen-396.body:
🖋️ **Mālik ibn Anas** said to a young man of Quraysh:

***“My nephew, learn **Adab** before you learn **knowledge**.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever seeks knowledge without first learning **Adab**, humility, and a right disposition often carries knowledge as a burden rather than as a blessing. **Adab preserves knowledge from becoming arrogance.**

malik-ibn-dinar-das-beste-dieser-dunya-4.title: 📖 The best of this Dunyā
malik-ibn-dinar-das-beste-dieser-dunya-4.body:
🖋️ **Mālik ibn Dīnār** رحمه الله said:

***“The people of the Dunyā left the Dunyā without having tasted the most delightful thing in it.”***

He was asked:

***“And what is that?”***

He replied:

***“The knowledge of the Exalted Allāh.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:**  
The most precious thing of this world does not lie in possession, status, or pleasure. Whoever knows the Exalted Allāh through His revelation, loves Him, and obeys Him has tasted the most delightful thing of the Dunyā. Whoever misses this may possess much and still lose the best.

malik-ibn-dinar-haerte-des-herzens-444.title: 📖 The gravest punishment is a hard heart
malik-ibn-dinar-haerte-des-herzens-444.body:
🖋️ **Mālik ibn Dīnār** رحمه الله said:

***“Among the punishments of the Exalted Allāh upon hearts and bodies are:***

***constraint in provision and weakness in worship.***

***And no servant was struck with a greater punishment than hardness of the heart.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:**  
Not every punishment is immediately visible. Among the most dangerous punishments is a hard heart that remains untouched by admonition, makes light of sin, and no longer feels humility in worship.

malik-istiva-ohne-wie-001.title: 📖 The Istiwāʾ is known – the how is unknown
malik-istiva-ohne-wie-001.body:
🖋️ **Mālik ibn Anas** said:

> ***“The Istiwāʾ is known, and the how is unknown.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The **Ahlus-Sunnah** affirm what Allah has reported about Himself, without denying the **Ṣifāt** and without asking about the how. In this lies the clear refutation of the **Jahmiyyah**: ***affirmation without Takyīf, without Tashbīh, and without Taʿṭīl.***

manhaj-bidah-beginnt-oft-mit-guter-absic.title: 📖 Manhaj: Bidʿah often begins with a good intention
manhaj-bidah-beginnt-oft-mit-guter-absic.body:
🖋️ **ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd** explained:

> ***“Ibn Masʿūd said to the people who were making new dhikr circles with pebbles: How many want the good but do not attain it.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** A good intention does not turn an innovation into the Sunnah. The Dīn is protected by transmission, not by feeling.

manhaj-der-sichere-weg-ist-die-sunnah-21.title: 📖 Manhaj: The safe path is the Sunnah
manhaj-der-sichere-weg-ist-die-sunnah-21.body:
🖋️ **ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz** explained:

> ***“ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote: Hold fast to the Sunnah, for with Allah’s permission it is a protection for you.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** When opinions, groups, and dispute increase, the Sunnah is not an addition, but rescue and protection.

manhaj-nicht-mit-ahl-al-ahwa-spielen-209.title: 📖 Manhaj: Do not play with Ahl al-Ahwāʾ
manhaj-nicht-mit-ahl-al-ahwa-spielen-209.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Sīrīn** explained:

> ***“When people of desires wanted to recite a verse to him, Ibn Sīrīn refused and said in substance: Either you stand up, or I stand up.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Not everyone who cites a verse is seeking guidance. Ahlus-Sunnah protects the heart from false interpretation and from people who confuse.

manhaj-wahrheit-ist-nicht-an-personen-ge.title: 📖 Manhaj: Truth is not bound to persons
manhaj-wahrheit-ist-nicht-an-personen-ge.body:
🖋️ **ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib** explained:

> ***“ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: Know the truth, then you will know its people.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ahlus-Sunnah measures men by the truth, not the truth by men. That protects against fanaticism and blind partisanship.

milde-schmueckt-jede-sache-175.title: 📖 Gentleness adorns every matter
milde-schmueckt-jede-sache-175.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said, or transmitted:

> ***“Gentleness is in nothing except that it adorns it; and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Rifq is not weakness, but beauty in leadership, family, Daʿwah, and correction.

miraj-ruyah-ikhtilaf-kein-pauschaler-tak.title: 📖 Miʿrāǧ, Ruʾyah, and blanket Takfīr – the documented Ikhtilāf
miraj-ruyah-ikhtilaf-kein-pauschaler-tak.body:
<!-- slide: 1 -->
# Miʿrāǧ with the body: the majority position

🖋️ Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله

“The majority of the Salaf and of the Muslims held that it took place with the body and in a waking state.”

He explains this view to be correct.

The affirmation of the real Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ with body and soul is thereby documented as the majority view of the Salaf and the Muslims.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ, Faṣl Ḥaqīqat al-Isrāʾ

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 2 -->
# The early scholars on the manner of the Isrāʾ

🖋️ Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ رحمه الله

“The Salaf and the scholars disagreed: did his Isrāʾ take place with his soul or with his body?”

He documents three transmitted views.

The majority position and this actual early Ikhtilāf are to be kept apart.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ, Ḥaqīqat al-Isrāʾ

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 3 -->
# The authentic wording of ʿĀʾišah

🖋️ ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها

“Whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ saw his Lord has uttered a tremendous false claim against Allah.”

The transmitted expression is: “faqad aʿẓama ʿalā Allāhi al-firyah”.

This report does not expressly state: “Whoever believes that is a Kāfir.” The wording must not be rewritten into another statement.

📝 Source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 177, report of ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 4 -->
# Ibn ʿAbbās: He saw Him with the heart

🖋️ ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

Concerning the verses “The heart did not lie about what it saw” and “Indeed, he saw Him another time,” he said:

“He saw Him with his heart twice.”

This is the heart-Ruʾyah authentically transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. It is not to be equated with an express claim about the bodily eyes.

📝 Source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176, from Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 5 -->
# Ibn Ḥaǧar: the documented Ruʾyah-Ikhtilāf

🖋️ Ibn Ḥaǧar رحمه الله

He documents various transmitted positions: ʿĀʾišah and Ibn Masʿūd denied the Ruʾyah; from Abū Ḏarr there were differing reports; another group affirmed it.

He also mentions the affirming statement of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and the transmission of ʿUrwah ibn az-Zubayr.

The classical sources treat this as a transmitted Ikhtilāf and not as a simple formula “Muslim or Kāfir”.

📝 Source: Ibn Ḥaǧar, Fatḥ al-Bārī, section on the Ikhtilāf of the Salaf concerning the Ruʾyah

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 6 -->
# Ibn Taymiyyah: heart-Ruʾyah and eye-Ruʾyah

🖋️ Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله

He affirms that it is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās in authentic reports:

“Muḥammad saw his Lord with his heart twice.”

At the same time he explains that no authentic express wording from Ibn ʿAbbās is established according to which he saw Him with his bodily eyes.

Therefore heart-Ruʾyah and eye-Ruʾyah must not be confused with one another.

📝 Source: Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 7 -->
# Two separate questions: Miʿrāǧ and Ruʾyah

The affirmation of the bodily Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ concerns the real ascent of the Prophet ﷺ.

The question of how the Ruʾyah is transmitted and understood is to be kept apart from that. The authentically reported heart-Ruʾyah is not automatically an eye-Ruʾyah either.

The bodily ascent must moreover not be understood as a claim of spatial co-location with Allah.

This distinction follows from the evidences named before.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176–177; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

<!-- slide: 8 -->
# Conclusion: no invented blanket Takfīr

The bodily Isrāʾ and Miʿrāǧ is documented as the majority view of the Salaf and the Muslims. Concerning the Ruʾyah, an actual Ikhtilāf was transmitted from the early scholars.

ʿĀʾišah رضي الله عنها denied the Ruʾyah sharply. Her authentic report does not, however, contain the express formula “Whoever believes this is a Kāfir.”

From Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما the heart-Ruʾyah is authentically transmitted.

The positions must not be mixed together or reformulated into a blanket Takfīr.

📝 Source: al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, aš-Šifāʾ; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 176–177; Ibn Ḥaǧar, Fatḥ al-Bārī; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā 6/509

[→ Source library Q36](/q/36/)

muhakamah-ablehnung-des-urteils-ist-able.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Rejecting the judgment is rejecting Allah’s sovereignty
muhakamah-ablehnung-des-urteils-ist-able.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** said:

> ***“Ibn Taymiyyah explained that returning to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ in dispute is an obligation, and that abandoning this contradicts Īmān.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The duty to return to the revelation is not theoretical. It is the measure of faith, obedience, and loyalty to the Dīn.

muhakamah-allahs-gesetz-wird-nicht-durch.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Allah’s law is not replaced by desire
muhakamah-allahs-gesetz-wird-nicht-durch.body:
🖋️ **aṭ-Ṭabarī** said:

> ***“aṭ-Ṭabarī explained Allah’s command to judge by what Allah has sent down, and not to follow their desires.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Hawā (desire) becomes dangerous when it is placed above judgment and right. Revelation sets right the heart and society.

muhakamah-das-urteil-der-jahiliyyah-324.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The judgment of the Jāhiliyyah
muhakamah-das-urteil-der-jahiliyyah-324.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained concerning ‘Do they seek the judgment of the Jāhiliyyah?’ that everything which departs from the judgment of Allah belongs to the judgment of the Jāhiliyyah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The judgment of Allah is perfect. Whoever knowingly places other standards above His revelation returns to a path of the Jāhiliyyah.

muhakamah-das-urteil-des-propheten-ist-v.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The judgment of the Prophet ﷺ is binding
muhakamah-das-urteil-des-propheten-ist-v.body:
🖋️ **ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“ash-Shāfiʿī explained that Allah has made following His Messenger ﷺ obligatory.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever rejects the judgment of the Messenger ﷺ does not reject a mere opinion. He contradicts the command of Allah.

muhakamah-der-hukm-gehoert-allah-allein-.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The Ḥukm belongs to Allah alone
muhakamah-der-hukm-gehoert-allah-allein-.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained concerning Allah’s statement ‘The Ḥukm belongs to Allah alone’ that command, decision, and disposal belong to Him alone.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Ḥukm is part of Tawḥīd. No human being may set himself above Allah’s right in legislation, decision, and obedience, or replace it.

muhakamah-der-streit-wird-zu-quran-und-s.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Dispute is brought back to Qurʾān and Sunnah
muhakamah-der-streit-wird-zu-quran-und-s.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained that the referral in dispute is to the Book of Allah and to the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The standard in dispute is not tribal feeling, party, custom, or the spirit of the age. The standard is revelation.

muhakamah-die-entscheidung-gehoert-allah.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The decision belongs to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ
muhakamah-die-entscheidung-gehoert-allah.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained that, after the judgment of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, no believer still has a choice of his own against that judgment.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Dīn is submission. When the judgment of revelation is clear, the heart’s choice against Allah and His Messenger ﷺ comes to an end.

muhakamah-die-herzen-muessen-das-urteil-.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Hearts must accept the judgment
muhakamah-die-herzen-muessen-das-urteil-.body:
🖋️ **Ibn al-Qayyim** said:

> ***“Ibn al-Qayyim explained that true submission lies in the heart not contradicting the judgment of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Muḥākamah is not only an outward dispute. The heart must love Allah’s judgment, accept it, and yield to it.

muhakamah-die-shariah-ist-gerechtigkeit-.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The Sharīʿah is justice and mercy
muhakamah-die-shariah-ist-gerechtigkeit-.body:
🖋️ **Ibn al-Qayyim** said:

> ***“Ibn al-Qayyim said in substance: The Sharīʿah is entirely justice, mercy, wisdom, and benefit.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever understands Allah’s law correctly recognizes in it not arbitrariness, but perfect justice, mercy, and wisdom.

muhakamah-gehorsam-gegenueber-gelehrten-.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Obedience to scholars has limits
muhakamah-gehorsam-gegenueber-gelehrten-.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** said:

> ***“Ibn Taymiyyah explained that obeying in the permitting of the forbidden and in the forbidding of the permitted can be a dangerous form of following besides Allah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Scholars are honored, but not deified. No human being may replace Allah’s Ḥalāl and Ḥarām.

muhakamah-gesetzgebung-ohne-erlaubnis-al.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Legislation without Allah’s permission
muhakamah-gesetzgebung-ohne-erlaubnis-al.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained, regarding ‘Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in the Dīn something that Allah has not permitted,’ that this is a rebuke of false legislation in the Dīn.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tashrīʿ in the Dīn belongs to Allah. Whoever gives religious legitimacy to what Allah has not permitted claims a dangerous right.

muhakamah-kein-iman-ohne-annahme-des-urt.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: No Īmān without accepting the judgment of the Prophet ﷺ
muhakamah-kein-iman-ohne-annahme-des-urt.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained that Allah swears by Himself: no one believes until he makes the Messenger ﷺ judge in disputes and submits completely.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Muḥākamah is not only the language of courts. It is the heart’s devotion to Allah’s revelation and to the judgment of His Messenger ﷺ.

muhakamah-kein-urteil-besser-als-allahs-.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: No judgment is better than Allah’s judgment
muhakamah-kein-urteil-besser-als-allahs-.body:
🖋️ **aṭ-Ṭabarī** said:

> ***“aṭ-Ṭabarī explained, regarding Allah’s statement ‘Who is better in judgment than Allah?’, the superiority and justice of Allah’s decision.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The believer recognizes: Allah’s judgment is more perfect, more just, and more knowing than any human system.

muhakamah-keine-vorziehung-vor-allah-und.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Nothing is placed before Allah and His Messenger ﷺ
muhakamah-keine-vorziehung-vor-allah-und.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained that the believers should not place anything before Allah and His Messenger ﷺ — neither a statement nor a deed.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever honors the Ḥukm of Allah places no opinion, no law, and no human being before Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

muhakamah-rabbi-und-gesetzgeber-sind-nic.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The Rabb and the Lawgiver are not to be separated
muhakamah-rabbi-und-gesetzgeber-sind-nic.body:
🖋️ **ash-Shanqīṭī** said:

> ***“ash-Shanqīṭī explained that it belongs to Allah’s right that He alone decides in legislation, and that no judgment is set equal to His judgment.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever acknowledges Allah as Lord may not give His right in the Ḥukm to a creature. Rubūbiyyah and legislation belong together.

muhakamah-taghut-beginnt-mit-uberschreit.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Tāghūt begins with transgressing the limit
muhakamah-taghut-beginnt-mit-uberschreit.body:
🖋️ **Ibn al-Qayyim** said:

> ***“Ibn al-Qayyim explained: Tāghūt is everything by which the servant transgresses his limit — whether something worshipped, followed, or obeyed.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tāghūt is not only a slogan. It denotes every transgression in which creatures displace Allah’s right.

muhakamah-taghut-urteil-wird-verworfen-3.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: The judgment of the Tāghūt is rejected
muhakamah-taghut-urteil-wird-verworfen-3.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr explained that the Āyah rebukes those who claim to believe but want to be directed to the Tāghūt for judgment.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Taḥākum to the Tāghūt is not a light matter. It contradicts the claim of Īmān when Allah’s judgment is deliberately abandoned.

muhakamah-wer-allahs-urteil-verlaesst-mu.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Whoever leaves Allah’s judgment must be judged with distinction
muhakamah-wer-allahs-urteil-verlaesst-mu.body:
🖋️ **Ibn al-Qayyim** said:

> ***“Ibn al-Qayyim distinguished between Kufr of action and Kufr of conviction, according to the state, the intention, and the inner approval.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The subject of Ḥukm is serious. But Takfīr upon specific persons requires conditions, impediments, and a correct distinction.

muhakamah-wer-anderes-urteil-schoener-fi.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Whoever finds another judgment finer
muhakamah-wer-anderes-urteil-schoener-fi.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Kathīr** said:

> ***“Ibn Kathīr rejected the Yāsiq of the Tātār, because in it mixed man-made judgments were put in the place of the Sharīʿah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever deliberately places man-made judgments above Allah’s law, or gives them religious equality, falls into grave danger.

muhakamah-wer-nicht-nach-allahs-offenbar.title: 📖 Muḥākamah: Whoever does not judge by Allah’s revelation
muhakamah-wer-nicht-nach-allahs-offenbar.body:
🖋️ **Ibn ʿAbbās** said:

> ***“Ibn ʿAbbās explained, regarding ‘Whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down,’ the well-known classification: it can be Kufr below Kufr.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Āyah is tremendous, but its application needs the rules of the Salaf: the difference between the deed, the state, Istihlāl, and the specific person.

muhammad-ibn-wasi-verborgene-traenen-453.title: 📖 The hidden tears of the righteous
muhammad-ibn-wasi-verborgene-traenen-453.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad b. Wāsiʿ** رحمه الله said:

***“I knew men who lay beside their wives with their heads on the same pillow — and the pillow became soaked with their tears without the wife noticing.***

***And I knew men who stood in the prayer row while tears ran down their cheeks, without the one beside them noticing.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True piety shows itself especially in what is hidden. The righteous concealed their tears and their good deeds from people, so that their worship belonged to Allah alone. A sincere heart grows soft in silence — without display, without praise, and without the desire to be seen by others.

mujahid-und-ein-zeuge-bedeutet-hukm-haki.title: 📖 Mujāhid: “And a witness…” means Ḥukm Ḥākim
mujahid-und-ein-zeuge-bedeutet-hukm-haki.body:
🖋️ **Mujāhid ibn Jabr and al-Farrāʾ** said:

> ***“The meaning of: ‘And a witness from her people testified’ is: the judgment of a judge.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever denies every judicial clarification in Yūsuf 12:26 ignores that early Tafsīr transmission expressly understood this as Ḥukm Ḥākim.

mukhlad-adab-vor-hadith-001.title: 📖 Adab before a great deal of knowledge
mukhlad-adab-vor-hadith-001.body:
🖋️ **Mukhlad ibn al-Ḥusayn** said to Ibn al-Mubārak:

> ***“We need much Adab more than much Hadith.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Knowledge** without **Adab** can make a person harsh, proud, and heedless. That is why the early Imāms did not attend only to collecting transmissions, but also to ***humility, conduct, and the effect of knowledge upon the heart***.

naehe-zum-propheten-durch-schoenen-chara.title: 📖 Nearness to the Prophet ﷺ through beautiful character
naehe-zum-propheten-durch-schoenen-chara.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said, or it was transmitted:

> ***“Among the most beloved to me, and those seated nearest to me on the Day of Resurrection, are the best of you in character.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Beautiful character is not a side topic. It is a path to nearness to the Prophet ﷺ and a protection against inflated speech and pride.

nafs-akhlaq-birr-ithm-nawwas-20261016-sl.title: 📖 The Nafs and true Aḫlāq
nafs-akhlaq-birr-ithm-nawwas-20261016-sl.body:
<!-- slide: 1 -->
# The Nafs and true Aḫlāq

🖋️ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"**Righteousness is good character.** And sin is that which stirs unrest in your **Nafs** and which you do not want people to know about."

Narrated by an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān رضي الله عنه.

📝 Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2553; Ǧāmiʿ at-Tirmiḏī 2389 (wording with "nafs").

[→ Original sources and direct references Q44](/q/44/)

<!-- slide: 2 -->
# Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī: The link between the Nafs and Aḫlāq

🖋️ Imām aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī رحمه الله explains in substance:

Good character and the inner calm of the Nafs belong together. The inner unrest that accompanies a sin stands against that.

He connects with this the transmissions about **righteousness and sin**. This is his explanation, not an additional prophetic wording.

📝 Aṭ-Ṭaḥāwī, Šarḥ Muškil al-Āṯār, vol. 5, pp. 385–388, no. 2138–2139.

[→ Original sources and direct references Q44](/q/44/)

<!-- slide: 3 -->
# Al-Baġawī: When the heart does not come to rest

🖋️ Imām al-Baġawī رحمه الله explains in substance the expression "what stirs in your Nafs":

It is something that **inwardly occupies the heart**, settles in it, and unsettles a person.

The explanation refers directly to the transmitted Ḥadīṯ.

📝 Al-Baġawī, Šarḥ as-Sunnah, vol. 13, pp. 77–78, no. 3494.

[→ Original sources and direct references Q44](/q/44/)

<!-- slide: 4 -->
# Al-Qurṭubī: Good character is more than friendliness

🖋️ Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qurṭubī رحمه الله mentions, among other things, regarding good character:

**Justice in dealings, gentleness in disputes, just judgment, and beneficence.**

Aḫlāq is thus not merely a friendly impression, but shows itself in concrete actions.

📝 Al-Qurṭubī, al-Mufhim, vol. 6, pp. 522–523.

[→ Original sources and direct references Q44](/q/44/)

<!-- slide: 5 -->
# Conclusion: Educate the Nafs, improve your character

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever wishes to educate his Nafs should also examine his conduct:

How do I speak with people? Am I just? Do I remain gentle when I disagree? Do I avoid what I would want to hide from others?

**Inner unrest is a warning sign, but no substitute for the Qurʾān and the authentic Sunnah.** The standard for the permitted and the forbidden remains revelation.

📝 A summary drawn from the texts named above; not an independent Ḥadīṯ or an independent scholarly quotation.

[→ Original sources and direct references Q44](/q/44/)

nichts-ist-schwerer-auf-der-waage-als-gu.title: 📖 Nothing is heavier on the Scale than good character
nichts-ist-schwerer-auf-der-waage-als-gu.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said, or it was transmitted:

> ***“Nothing is heavier on the Scale than good character.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever wants to fill his scale must not belittle Akhlāq. Beautiful words, patience, gentleness, and just dealings are weighty deeds.

nuzul-allahs-ist-haqq-424.title: 📖 The Nuzūl of Allah is Haqq
nuzul-allahs-ist-haqq-424.body:
🖋️ **Zuhayr ibn ʿAbbād** reported about the Imāms whom he reached:

***“Every one of the scholars I reached — Mālik, Sufyān, Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, ʿĪsā, Ibn al-Mubārak, and Wakīʿ — used to say: The Nuzūl of Allah is Haqq.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** The early Imāms affirmed the Nuzūl of Allah, because it is authentically transmitted. They accepted this attribute without reinterpreting it, without denying it, without asking how, and without comparing Allah to creation.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Nuzūl of Allah is Haqq with Ahlus-Sunnah. One affirms it as it was transmitted, and leaves the how to Allah.

osmanen-khilafah-der-nubuwwah-116.title: 📖 The Ottomans ≠ the Khilāfah of the Nubuwwah
osmanen-khilafah-der-nubuwwah-116.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ, an-Nawawī, and al-ʿAynī** said:

> ***“The Khilāfah of the Nubuwwah lasts thirty years; thereafter Allah gives kingship to whom He wills.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Not every great Muslim state is automatically Khilāfah an-Nubuwwah. The texts distinguish between Khilāfah and Mulk, and they bind the Imāmah Kubrā in principle to Quraysh.

prophet-dunya-konkurrenz-ummah-548.title: 📖 I do not fear poverty for you
prophet-dunya-konkurrenz-ummah-548.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

***“By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you. Rather, I fear that the Dunyā will be spread out for you as it was spread out for those before you; then you will compete for it as they competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The greatest danger is not always scarcity, but when the **Dunyā** fills the heart, until the **Ākhirah**, death, the grave, and the reckoning are forgotten. The believer uses wealth, but does not let wealth possess his heart.

qatadah-tarbiyyah-familie-tahrim-66-6-20.title: 📖 True Tarbiyyah — upbringing is a responsibility
qatadah-tarbiyyah-familie-tahrim-66-6-20.body:
🖋️ **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah** رحمه الله explained Qurʾān 66:6 in meaning:

> "One protects one’s family by calling them to **obedience to Allah**, holding them back from **disobedience**, and **helping them to fulfill Allah’s commands**."

🌙 **Conclusion:** True Tarbiyyah does not mean merely teaching children rules. It means guiding them to obedience to Allah, guarding them from sins, and actively helping them on this path.

quran-24-22-vergeben-und-nachsicht-20261.title: 📖 Forgiveness — who would not wish for it?
quran-24-22-vergeben-und-nachsicht-20261.body:
🖋️ **Allah ʿazza wa jalla** says:

> “They should **forgive and show forbearance**. Do you not love that **Allah forgive you**? And Allah is All-Forgiving and Merciful.”

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever wishes for Allah’s forgiveness should himself be ready to forgive others. True greatness is also shown in not abandoning good after having suffered wrong.

rabiah-istiwa-nicht-unbekannt-134.title: 📖 Istiwaʾ is not unknown
rabiah-istiwa-nicht-unbekannt-134.body:
🖋️ **Rabīʿah** said:

> ***“Istiwaʾ is not unknown, and the Kayfiyyah is not graspable; from Allah is the message, upon the Messenger is the conveyance, and upon us is faith.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The statement of **Rabīʿah** shows the way of **Ahlus-Sunnah**: the meaning of ***Istiwaʾ*** is not denied and is not declared wholly unknown; what is unknown is the **Kayfiyyah**. This is therefore a clear refutation of **Tafwīḍ** in the sense of a total negation of the meaning.

recht-zuruckholen-ist-nicht-automatisch-.title: 📖 Recovering a right is not automatically Taḥākum to the Ṭāġūt
recht-zuruckholen-ist-nicht-automatisch-.body:
🖋️ **al-Māwardī** explained:

> ***“al-Māwardī said: One form is that he is able to take his right from him through Muḥākamah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Fiqh distinguishes between the intended Ṭāġūt judgment and the recovery of a withheld right. Whoever equates all of it destroys the precision of the Fuqahāʾ.

recht-zurueckholen-nicht-automatisch-sch.title: 📖 Recovering a right is not automatically Shirk Akbar
recht-zurueckholen-nicht-automatisch-sch.body:
🖋️ **al-Māwardī** said about recovering a withheld right:

> ***“One of the two forms is that he is able to take his right from him through Muḥākamah.”***

This statement does not stand in a chapter on Shirk, but in the Fiqh chapter on taking one’s own right from someone who withholds it.

🖋️ The Fuqahāʾ likewise distinguished between the forbidden seeking of the Ṭāġūt judgment and the repelling of wrong, or the recovery of one’s own right.

> ***A complaint, a lawsuit, or a demand for return is not automatically Kufr Akbar or Shirk Akbar, so long as one does not take Bāṭil and does not prefer the Ṭāġūt judgment to the judgment of Allah.***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The direct Ṭāġūt text condemns the intended Ṭāġūt judgment and Riḍā with it instead of with the judgment of Allah. The recovery of a withheld right, by contrast, was treated by the Fuqahāʾ as its own subject of Fiqh: **Muḥākamah, Daʿāwā, Bayyināt, Aḫdh al-Ḥaqq, and Dafʿ aẓ-Ẓulm**.

recht-zurueckholen-nicht-automatisch-shi.title: 📖 Recovering a right is not automatically Shirk Akbar
recht-zurueckholen-nicht-automatisch-shi.body:
<!-- slide: 1 -->
# Is recovering a right automatically Shirk Akbar?

This question needs a clean distinction:

Not every complaint, lawsuit, or demand for one’s own right is automatically Shirk Akbar.

What is decisive is whether someone only recovers his right — or whether he wants the Ṭāġūt judgment itself, affirms it, and is pleased with it.

Recovering a right is not the same as Riḍā with the Ṭāġūt judgment.

📝 Source: Summary of the following evidences.

<!-- slide: 2 -->
# The direct Ṭāġūt text

aṭ-Ṭabarī explained, regarding “they want to be referred to the Ṭāġūt,” that the blamed case is when, in a dispute, one turns to the Ṭāġūt, acts according to his word, and is pleased with his judgment — instead of with the judgment of الله.

What is blamed is the Ṭāġūt judgment that is wanted, taken as authoritative, and accepted with pleasure.

📝 Source: aṭ-Ṭabarī, Ǧāmiʿ al-Bayān, tafsīr of Sūrah an-Nisāʾ 4:60.

<!-- slide: 3 -->
# The false leap

It does not follow from this that every outward complaint, every lawsuit, or every demand for a right automatically falls under Shirk Akbar.

What is blamed is the case in which someone wants the Ṭāġūt judgment itself, takes it as authoritative, and is pleased with it — instead of with the judgment of الله.

A complaint is not automatically Riḍā with the Ṭāġūt.

📝 Source: Derived from aṭ-Ṭabarī’s explanation of Sūrah an-Nisāʾ 4:60.

<!-- slide: 4 -->
# A right through Muḥākamah

al-Māwardī said:

“One of the two forms is that he is able to take his right from him through Muḥākamah.”

This statement does not stand in the chapter on Shirk, but in the chapter:

“That a man takes his right from the one who withholds it from him.”

The Fuqahāʾ treated the recovery of a right as its own subject of Fiqh.

📝 Source: al-Māwardī, al-Ḥāwī al-Kabīr, Bāb Aḫḏ ar-Raǧul Ḥaqqahu Mimman Yamnaʿuhu Iyyāh, vol. 17, p. 412.

<!-- slide: 5 -->
# Judge, Sulṭān, and repelling

Ibn Qudāmah said:

“If he can recover it through the judge or the Sulṭān, then he is not permitted to take it by another way.”

He also mentioned the case in which the other denies the right, no proof is available, or he does not appear for the Muḥākamah.

Ibn Taymiyyah distinguished between inflicting wrong and repelling wrong.

📝 Source: Ibn Qudāmah, al-Muġnī, Kitāb ad-Daʿāwā wa-l-Bayyināt, vol. 10, pp. 275–276; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā, vol. 30, pp. 339–340.

<!-- slide: 6 -->
# Bāṭil remains forbidden

The Prophet ﷺ said:

“Whoever is awarded something of his brother’s right, let him not take it; for by that I only cut off for him a piece of the Fire.”

A false judgment does not make Bāṭil permissible.

Even if an authority awards something to someone, he may not thereby take another’s right.

📝 Source: Mālik, al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Kitāb al-Aqḍiyah; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, at-Tamhīd, vol. 22.

<!-- slide: 7 -->
# The clear boundary

A complaint, a lawsuit, or a demand is not automatically Kufr Akbar or Shirk Akbar when one only claims back one’s own right and repels wrong.

It becomes dangerous when one affirms the Ṭāġūt judgment, prefers it to the judgment of الله, has Riḍā with it, or takes Bāṭil through the procedure.

Aḫḏ al-Ḥaqq is not the same as Riḍā with the Ṭāġūt judgment.

🌙 Conclusion: Recovering one’s own right is not the same as affirming, preferring, or being pleased with a Ṭāġūt judgment.

📝 Source: Summary of the evidences above: aṭ-Ṭabarī on 4:60; al-Māwardī, al-Ḥāwī; Ibn Qudāmah, al-Muġnī; Ibn Taymiyyah, Maǧmūʿ al-Fatāwā; Mālik and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr.

refutation-089-quran-kalam-allah-ghayr-m.title: 📖 The Qurʾān is the Word of Allah
refutation-089-quran-kalam-allah-ghayr-m.body:
🖋️ **ʿAmr ibn Dīnār** said:

> ***“I met nine Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they said: Whoever says that the Qurʾān is created is a Kāfir.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The foundation of Ahlus-Sunnah is clear: **The Qurʾān is the Word of Allah**, not a created word. In this lies the refutation of the Jahmiyyah.

refutation-090-tabari-quran-makhluq.title: 📖 Whoever calls the Qurʾān created
refutation-090-tabari-quran-makhluq.body:
🖋️ **Abū Jaʿfar aṭ-Ṭabarī** said:

> ***“Whoever says with conviction that the Qurʾān is created is a Kāfir.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The early Imāms did not treat the statement **“the Qurʾān is created”** as a light wording, but as a principle of the Jahmiyyah.

refutation-091-lafziyyah-jahmiyyah.title: 📖 The trap of the Lafẓiyyah
refutation-091-lafziyyah-jahmiyyah.body:
🖋️ **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** said:

> ***“The Lafẓiyyah are Jahmiyyah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ahlus-Sunnah also close the **hidden paths to the Jahmiyyah**. Whoever sidesteps the truth opens the door to distortion.

refutation-092-abu-ubayd-quran-birammati.title: 📖 The Qurʾān in its entirety
refutation-092-abu-ubayd-quran-birammati.body:
🖋️ **Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām** said:

> ***“The Qurʾān, in its entirety, is not created.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Not only individual meanings, but **the Qurʾān as a whole** is the Word of Allah. Thus the door of the Jahmiyyah is closed.

refutation-093-ahl-al-kalam-la-yuflihoun.title: 📖 The people of Kalām have no success
refutation-093-ahl-al-kalam-la-yuflihoun.body:
🖋️ **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** said:

> ***“Good. The people of Kalām will not succeed.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The way of Ahlus-Sunnah is **revelation and Athar**, not philosophical terms placed above the Qurʾān and the Sunnah.

refutation-094-allah-mutakallim.title: 📖 Allah speaks
refutation-094-allah-mutakallim.body:
🖋️ **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** said:

> ***“Allah has always been knowing and speaking; the Qurʾān is the Word of Allah, not created.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever negates Allah’s speech contradicts the way of the Imāms. **Allah speaks**, as befits His majesty.

refutation-095-nuzul-bila-kayf.title: 📖 The Nuzūl without the question of how
refutation-095-nuzul-bila-kayf.body:
🖋️ **Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** said:

> ***“Let the Ḥadīth proceed as it was transmitted: without the question of how and without a limit.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Sunnah is **affirmed**, not erased by Taʾwīl. This is the safe path against the Jahmiyyah and the Muʿaṭṭilah.

refutation-096-istiwa-ohne-takyif.title: 📖 Istiwaʾ without Takyīf
refutation-096-istiwa-ohne-takyif.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar** said:

> ***“It is enough here to say: Allah is above the Throne, without Takyīf.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ahlus-Sunnah affirm **Istiwaʾ**, without likening and without the question of how. In this lies the middle between Taʿṭīl and Tashbīh.

refutation-097-ruyah-bila-kayf.title: 📖 The Ruʾyah is affirmed
refutation-097-ruyah-bila-kayf.body:
🖋️ **al-Awzāʿī, Sufyān ath-Thawrī, Mālik ibn Anas, and al-Layth ibn Saʿd** said:

> ***“Let them pass as they came — without the question of how.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The narrations about the **Ruʾyah** are not rejected and not twisted. They are accepted as they came.

refutation-098-ibn-uyaynah-jahmi.title: 📖 Whoever denies the Qurʾān and the Ruʾyah
refutation-098-ibn-uyaynah-jahmi.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah** said:

> ***“Whoever does not say that the Qurʾān is the Word of Allah and that Allah will be seen in Paradise is a Jahmī.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Two signs of the Jahmiyyah are clear: **denial of the Qurʾān as the Word of Allah** and **denial of the Ruʾyah**.

sabr-und-sieg-001.title: 📖 Victory is with patience
sabr-und-sieg-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Know: Victory is with patience, relief is with distress, and with difficulty comes relief.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever has **Tawakkul** does not despair in constriction. For Allah brings ***relief*** after distress and a way after patience.

salman-gib-jedem-sein-recht-451.title: 📖 Give everyone his right
salman-gib-jedem-sein-recht-451.body:
🖋️ **Salmān al-Fārisī رضي الله عنه** said to Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه:

***“Your Lord has a **right** over you, your soul has a **right** over you, and your family has a **right** over you. So give everyone who possesses a right ***his right***.”***

When Abū ad-Dardāʾ رضي الله عنه reported this to the Prophet ﷺ, he said:

***“Salmān has spoken the truth.”***

Salmān رضي الله عنه was not thereby correcting an obligatory act of worship, but an exaggeration in voluntary deeds through which other existing rights were neglected.

True piety does not consist in fulfilling one area especially strongly while disregarding the rights of the body or of the family. The Muslim fulfills **Allah’s right** and at the same time gives everyone what is rightfully due to him.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The straight path is a path of ***balance and justice***: give your Lord, your soul, and your family each their right, without neglecting one right at the expense of another.

schlechter-verdacht-zerstoert-bruederlic.title: 📖 Bad suspicion destroys brotherhood
schlechter-verdacht-zerstoert-bruederlic.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said, or transmitted:

> ***“Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Not every inner supposition deserves to be believed. Whoever feeds suspicion opens doors to spying, hatred, and separation.

selbst-der-bissen-fuer-die-ehefrau-wird-.title: 📖 Even the morsel for the wife is rewarded
selbst-der-bissen-fuer-die-ehefrau-wird-.body:
🖋️ **Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ رضي الله عنه** reported:

**The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:**

***“You will not make any expenditure by which you seek the pleasure of Allah without being rewarded for it — even for what you place in the mouth of your wife.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Through a sincere **Niyyah**, even the everyday provision of the wife becomes a rewarded deed. No permissible expenditure by which the pleasure of Allah is sought is lost with Him.

shafii-buch-widerspricht-sunnah-001.title: 📖 When my book contradicts the Sunnah
shafii-buch-widerspricht-sunnah-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“If you find in my book something that contradicts the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then follow it and leave what I have said.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Fiqh** is not set against the Sunnah. The safe path is to measure the words of the Imāms by ***Qurʾān, Sunnah, and Athar***.

shafii-debatte-als-nasiha-001.title: 📖 Debate as Naṣīḥah
shafii-debatte-als-nasiha-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“I have never debated with anyone except on the basis of Naṣīḥah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Debate in the **Dīn** must not be for victory, ego, or exposure. True **Naṣīḥah** seeks ***truth, correction, and the salvation of the heart***.

shafii-drei-grundlagen-des-wissens-001.title: 📖 Three foundations of knowledge
shafii-drei-grundlagen-des-wissens-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“Knowledge becomes beautiful only through three things: Taqwā before Allah, attaining the Sunnah, and Khashyah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Knowledge** needs more than sharpness of mind. It needs ***Taqwā, the Sunnah, and fear of Allah***, so that it becomes light.

shafii-ich-wollte-seine-rechtleitung-001.title: 📖 I wanted his guidance
shafii-ich-wollte-seine-rechtleitung-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“I have never debated with anyone except that I wished that he be guided, made firm, and supported.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **Adab** in discussion is shown in that one does not want the other’s fall, but ***his right guidance***.

shafii-iman-wort-und-tat-001.title: 📖 Īmān is word and deed
shafii-iman-wort-und-tat-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“Īmān is word and deed; it increases and decreases.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The **Aqīdah** of Ahlus-Sunnah does not separate Īmān from action. Īmān is ***affirmation, deed, and change*** — it grows and becomes weaker.

shafii-keine-zuschreibung-zu-mir-001.title: 📖 Knowledge without fame
shafii-keine-zuschreibung-zu-mir-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“I wished that people would learn this knowledge without anything of it being attributed to me.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Ikhlāṣ** shows itself when a person loves the benefit of the truth, even when his own name remains hidden in that.

shafii-schmuck-des-wissens-001.title: 📖 The adornment of knowledge
shafii-schmuck-des-wissens-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“The adornment of knowledge is Waraʿ and Ḥilm.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Knowledge** is made beautiful by **Waraʿ** and **Ḥilm**. Without fear of Allah and gentleness, knowledge can become harsh and lose its true benefit.

shafii-sunnah-vor-meinem-wort-001.title: 📖 The Sunnah stands above my word
shafii-sunnah-vor-meinem-wort-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“Everything that I said, if something authentic from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ contradicts it, then that takes precedence — and do not follow me blindly.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Imāms are honored, but the **Sunnah** stands above every human word. True **Ittibāʿ** is ***attachment to the proof***.

shafii-taten-und-worte-001.title: 📖 What counts are deeds and words
shafii-taten-und-worte-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“Allah has pardoned what is in the hearts, and deeds and words were recorded for people.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** A person is not burdened with mere inner thoughts, so long as they do not become **word** or **deed**. In this lies mercy — and at the same time responsibility for ***speech and action***.

shafii-wissen-das-nuetzt-001.title: 📖 Knowledge is that which benefits
shafii-wissen-das-nuetzt-001.body:
🖋️ **Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ash-Shāfiʿī** said:

> ***“Knowledge is not that which is memorized; knowledge is that which benefits.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **knowledge** shows itself not only in memory, but in ***benefit, action, and change of the heart***.

shirk-durch-anrufung-der-toten-und-abwes.title: 📖 Shirk by calling upon the dead and the absent
shirk-durch-anrufung-der-toten-und-abwes.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** explained:

> ***“Ibn Taymiyyah said: Whoever calls upon creatures among the dead and the absent and seeks help from them is an innovator in the Dīn and commits Shirk with the Lord of the worlds.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Duʿāʾ is ʿIbādah (worship). When it is given to the dead or the absent, something of Allah’s right is transferred to creatures.

shirk-in-der-not-die-hilfe-gehort-allah-.title: 📖 Shirk in distress: help belongs to Allah alone
shirk-in-der-not-die-hilfe-gehort-allah-.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** explained:

> ***“Ibn Taymiyyah explained that the Muslims, in times of distress, call upon Allah alone and do not refer their needs back to anyone else.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Distress is a test of Tawḥīd. Precisely when a person is weak, it becomes clear whether his heart calls upon Allah alone.

shirk-ist-der-grote-ungehorsam-205.title: 📖 Shirk is the greatest disobedience
shirk-ist-der-grote-ungehorsam-205.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** explained:

> ***“Ibn Taymiyyah said: Shirk with Allah is the greatest sin by which Allah is disobeyed.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever trivializes Shirk does not trivialize a side issue, but the greatest breach in Allah’s right over His servants.

shirk-wenn-der-mittler-angerufen-wird-20.title: 📖 Shirk: when the intermediary is called upon
shirk-wenn-der-mittler-angerufen-wird-20.body:
🖋️ **Ibn Taymiyyah** explained:

> ***“Whoever makes the angels and the prophets into intermediaries, calls upon them, relies upon them, and asks them for benefit and the removal of harm, is a Kāfir by the consensus of the Muslims.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The permissible asking of a living person for Duʿāʾ is something other than calling upon angels, prophets, or the dead in matters that only Allah is able to do.

sifat-allah-dahik-ohne-takyif-001.title: 📖 Allah’s laughter is affirmed
sifat-allah-dahik-ohne-takyif-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Allah laughs at two men: one kills the other, and both enter Paradise.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Ahlus-Sunnah** affirm what has come authentically concerning the **Ṣifāt of Allah**, without ***Takyīf***, without ***Tashbīh***, and without ***Taʿṭīl***. The **Jahmiyyah** denied such texts, but the Imāms held fast to the transmitted Sunnah.

sifat-allah-yad-adam-001.title: 📖 Allah created Ādam with His Hand
sifat-allah-yad-adam-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** reported in the Hadith about the dispute between Ādam and Mūsā:

> ***“You are Ādam, whom Allah created with His Hand and into whom He breathed of His spirit.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Ahlus-Sunnah** affirm the transmitted **Ṣifāt of Allah** without ***Takyīf***, without ***Tashbīh***, and without ***Taʿṭīl***. The mention of the **Hand of Allah** is not denied and not reinterpreted, but affirmed as it corresponds to the revelation.

sifat-allah-yamin-allah-001.title: 📖 Allah’s Right Hand is full
sifat-allah-yamin-allah-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Allah’s Right Hand is full; no expenditure diminishes it. It gives abundantly by night and by day.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Ahlus-Sunnah** affirm what has come authentically concerning the **Ṣifāt of Allah**, without ***Takyīf***, without ***Tashbīh***, and without ***Taʿṭīl***. In this lies the refutation of the **Jahmiyyah**, who wanted to nullify such texts through denial and reinterpretation.

sprich-gutes-oder-schweige-172.title: 📖 Speak good or remain silent
sprich-gutes-oder-schweige-172.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said, or it was transmitted:

> ***“Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The tongue is a gate to reward or burden. Silence is not weakness when the word carries no benefit.

statement-0005-imam-malik-ummah-salaf-46.title: 📖 That by which the Ummah is set right again
statement-0005-imam-malik-ummah-salaf-46.body:
🖋️ **Imām Mālik ibn Anas (رحمه الله) said:**

***“The latter part of this Ummah will not be set right except by that by which its first part was set right.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:**
**The Ummah is not renewed through new paths, modern inventions or distant standards**, but through the same light that raised its beginning: **the Qurʾān, the Sunnah and holding fast to the way of the Salaf.**

sue-des-iman-durch-liebe-fur-allah-232.title: 📖 The sweetness of Īmān through love for Allah
sue-des-iman-durch-liebe-fur-allah-232.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said in meaning: Whoever loves Allah and His Messenger more than everything else, and loves someone only for Allah, finds the sweetness of Īmān.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Love in the Dīn is not mere nearness to people. It becomes pure when it is for Allah and serves Īmān.

sufyan-ath-thawri-fremde-rechte-zurueckg.title: 📖 First repair the wrong — then increase the dhikr
sufyan-ath-thawri-fremde-rechte-zurueckg.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī** رحمه الله was asked:

“A man has **acquired 30,000 dirhams wrongfully** and says: I will say tasbīḥ, taḥmīd and takbīr until I have gathered just as many good deeds. What do you say to that?”

He answered:

“**He should return the money first.** For his dhikr will not be accepted until he has returned it.”

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Returning the rights of others** cannot be replaced by additional voluntary acts of worship. Whoever has committed wrong must strive for **restitution**.

sufyan-ath-thawri-gewissheit-allah-nicht.title: 📖 Certainty means not accusing Allāh
sufyan-ath-thawri-gewissheit-allah-nicht.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** رحمه الله said:

***“Certainty is that you do not accuse your Lord concerning anything that befalls you.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:**
True certainty shows itself in that the servant accepts Allāh’s decree and does not accuse his Lord on account of trials.

sufyan-ath-thawri-handle-nach-dem-wissen.title: 📖 Sufyān ath-Thawrī: Act upon knowledge
sufyan-ath-thawri-handle-nach-dem-wissen.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** said:

> ***“Sufyān ath-Thawrī said in meaning: Knowledge calls to action; if it is answered, it remains, otherwise it departs.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Knowledge without action becomes a burden. Whoever receives Allah’s knowledge should preserve it with obedience.

sufyan-ath-thawri-wenig-essen-und-wenig-.title: 📖 Sufyān ath-Thawrī: Little food and little sleep strengthen the heart
sufyan-ath-thawri-wenig-essen-und-wenig-.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** said:

> ***“Sufyān ath-Thawrī warned against excessive eating and sleep, and he linked strength of the heart with restraint.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tazkiyyah often begins with hidden habits. Whoever wants his heart must restrain his desires.

sufyan-ath-thawri-wissen-erleichterung-v.title: 📖 True knowledge is not mere severity
sufyan-ath-thawri-wissen-erleichterung-v.body:
🖋️ **Imām Sufyān ath-Thawrī** رحمه الله said:

***“Knowledge, with us, is the facilitation that comes from a trustworthy person; as for severity, everyone masters it.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:**
Not everyone who is severe possesses fiqh. True knowledge is recognized in that it speaks with trust, proof and maturity — not with harshness without insight.

sufyan-ibn-uyaynah-zuhd-001.title: 📖 Zuhd between gratitude and patience
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah-zuhd-001.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah** was asked: “What is zuhd in the dunyā?” He said:

> ***“When Allah grants him a favor, he is grateful; and when he is tried with an affliction, he is patient — that is zuhd.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **zuhd** is not only poverty or outward simplicity. It shows itself in that the heart does not become arrogant at a **favor** and does not collapse at a **trial**: ***shukr in blessing and ṣabr in trial.***

sufyan-schmueckt-wissen-nicht-sich-selbs.title: 📖 Knowledge instead of self-display
sufyan-schmueckt-wissen-nicht-sich-selbs.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** رحمه الله said:

“**Adorn knowledge through yourselves**, and do ***not adorn yourselves*** with knowledge.”

🌙 **Conclusion:** **True knowledge** does not serve reputation. Its worth shows itself in ***sincerity, humility and lived adab***, not in adorning oneself with it before others.

sufyan-thawri-iman-athar-001.title: 📖 Īmān is word, deed and intention
sufyan-thawri-iman-athar-001.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** said:

> ***“Īmān is word, deed and intention. It increases and decreases: it increases through obedience and decreases through sin.”***

> ***“Word, deed and intention are valid only when they agree with the Sunnah.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation**

This statement shows a clear principle of **Ahl as-Sunnah**: **Īmān** is not merely a word on the tongue, nor merely an inward claim in the heart. Rather, **word**, **deed** and **intention** belong to it.

It likewise becomes clear here: Īmān is not the same in all people. It grows stronger through **obedience** and is weakened through **sins**. For this reason the early Imāms did not join ʿaqīdah to empty claims, but to **following**, the **Sunnah** and righteous deed.

Especially important is the last sentence: even word, deed and intention need **agreement with the Sunnah**. A deed does not become right because a person finds it good, but because it agrees with the transmitted way.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever wants to understand **Īmān** rightly must not separate it from the **Sunnah**. True Īmān shows itself in **word**, **deed**, **intention** and in holding fast to the way which the early Imāms transmitted.

sufyan-thawri-niyyah-struggle-20261008-4.title: 📖 The hardest struggle is one’s own intention
sufyan-thawri-niyyah-struggle-20261008-4.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān aṯ-Ṯawrī** (رحمه الله) said:

> "I struggled with nothing **more severely** than with my **intention**, for it keeps changing with me again and again."

🌙 **Conclusion:** Even the great scholars of the Salaf struggled to keep their **niyyah** pure. Not only our deeds need attention, but also the intention with which we perform them.

sufyan-thawri-zuhd-001.title: 📖 Zuhd is short hope
sufyan-thawri-zuhd-001.body:
🖋️ **Sufyān ath-Thawrī** said:

> ***“Zuhd in the dunyā does not mean wearing coarse clothing or eating plain food. Rather, zuhd in the dunyā is: short hope.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **zuhd** is not merely outward appearance, but a heart that does not plan the **dunyā** without end and does not forget the **ākhirah**.

sulayman-ibn-suhman-julus-tajsim-buhtan-.title: 📖 Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān on Ǧulūs, the Tajsīm accusation and Buhtān
sulayman-ibn-suhman-julus-tajsim-buhtan-.body:
🖋️ **Sulaymān ibn Suḥmān رحمه الله said:**

***"If this is established from the Imāms of the people of Islam, then the opposition of the rabble, who resemble cattle, carries no weight."***

**فَإِذَا ثَبَتَ هَذَا عَنْ أَئِمَّةِ أَهْلِ الْإِسْلَامِ، فَلَا عِبْرَةَ بِمَنْ خَالَفَهُمْ مِنَ الطَّغَامِ أَشْبَاهِ الْأَنْعَامِ.**

Ibn Suḥmān brings this statement in connection with the transmitted reports about **Ǧulūs** and the early Imāms, who passed these reports on and did not reject them solely because of their content.

His argument is directed against the one who disparages the carriers of such transmissions wholesale as Mušabbihah or Muǧassimah. For him the standard is not the later slogans of the people of Kalām, but the way the early Imāms dealt with the transmitted texts.

Two questions must be distinguished here: Ibn Suḥmān defends the Imāms against the blanket accusation of Tajsīm. The independent isnād-critical assessment of each individual Ǧulūs report is not thereby automatically decided.

## The consequence of the blanket Tajsīm accusation

At a later place Ibn Suḥmān replies to the claim that affirming the revealed attributes of Allah necessarily leads to Tajsīm and to the veneration of a bodily idol.

***"If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his Companions, those who followed them in goodness, Ahl as-Sunnah wa-l-Ǧamāʿah from the people of Ḥadīṯ, and other exemplary Imāms described Allah with that by which He described Himself and by which His Messenger described Him, then, in the view of this misguided Mulḥid, they would have worshipped an idol because of these consequences — consequences which the earlier philosophers invented and which their heirs among the Mutakallimūn took over, those who left the path of the believers. The curse of Allah be upon the wrongdoers."***

Ibn Suḥmān by no means claims that the Messenger ﷺ or the Salaf actually worshipped an idol. Rather, he lays open the **necessary consequence of his opponent’s argumentation**:

Whoever, on the basis of philosophically constructed consequences, calls every affirmation of ʿUluw, Istiwāʾ, Ruʾyah and the other revealed Ṣifāt Tajsīm or idolatry, ultimately directs this accusation against those who first transmitted and affirmed these texts.

The error lies in placing ambiguous philosophical terms and invented rational consequences above the texts of the Qurʾān and the Sunnah. Precisely this procedure is what Ibn Suḥmān rejects.

## Buhtān against the Imāms

In *Kašf Ġayāhib aẓ-Ẓalām*, Ibn Suḥmān replies to invented accusations against Šayḫ Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله.

***"It is out of the question for us to say such a thing. Glory be to You! This is a mighty slander. How can such a word come forth from their mouths, while they lie deliberately? Its falsehood is known by necessity. No one who possesses even the slightest knowledge of the state of the exemplary Imāms doubts this. Whoever reads the books, writings and letters of the Šayḫ and considers his course of life and his call to Allah, it becomes clear to him that this belongs to the lies and slanders."***

Ibn Suḥmān thereby sets a clear standard: the ʿaqīdah of a scholar is not judged by the claims of his opponents, but by his **verifiable books, letters, statements and his known work**.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ibn Suḥmān clearly distinguishes between **Iṯbāt and Tamṯīl**: the revealed Ṣifāt are affirmed, without equating Allah to the creatures or asking about the how. Blanket accusations of Tajsīm and invented accusations against the Imāms are, for him, not proof, but open **Buhtān**.

tagut-ist-eine-falsche-autoritat-201.title: 📖 Ṭāġūt is a false authority
tagut-ist-eine-falsche-autoritat-201.body:
🖋️ **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** explained:

> ***“Mujāhid explained: The Ṭāġūt is the Shayṭān in the form of a human being, to whom they let themselves be directed; and he is the bearer of their affair.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Ṭāġūt is a false authority that draws people away from the judgment of Allah. Therefore kufr bi-ṭ-Ṭāġūt is a principle of Tawḥīd.

tagut-urteil-willentlich-zu-suchen-ist-d.title: 📖 Willingly seeking the Ṭāġūt judgment is the blameworthy case
tagut-urteil-willentlich-zu-suchen-ist-d.body:
🖋️ **aṭ-Ṭabarī** explained:

> ***“aṭ-Ṭabarī mentioned the case in which one wanted, in a dispute, to turn to the kāhin, although the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among them.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The dangerous point is wanting the judgment of the Ṭāġūt and turning away from the judgment of Allah and of His Messenger ﷺ.

tagut-wenn-urteil-beim-kahin-gesucht-wir.title: 📖 Ṭāġūt: when judgment is sought from the kāhin
tagut-wenn-urteil-beim-kahin-gesucht-wir.body:
🖋️ **aṭ-Ṭabarī** explained:

> ***“aṭ-Ṭabarī transmitted, in the explanation of 4:60, that by the Ṭāġūt in this case the kāhin is meant, to whom one wanted to be directed.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Qurʾān does not merely rebuke an outward procedure, but the will to put the judgment of the Ṭāġūt in the place of revelation.

takfir-auf-imam-ahmad-und-imam-ash-shafi.title: 📖 Takfīr upon Imām Aḥmad and Imām ash-Shāfiʿī?
takfir-auf-imam-ahmad-und-imam-ash-shafi.body:
🖋️ **Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal** said:

> ***“If you see a man who loves Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, then know: he is a man of the Sunnah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Whoever brings down Aḥmad and ash-Shāfiʿī sets himself against the standards of the great naqqād and Imāms who carried them as pillars of the Sunnah.

takfir-bil-umum-399.title: 📖 Quss ibn Saʿīdah: Barāʾah from shirk
takfir-bil-umum-399.body:
🖋️ **From Quss ibn Saʿīdah al-Iyādī** it is transmitted:

***“Truly, Allah has a religion that is more beloved to Him than your religion, upon which you stand.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** This statement shows **barāʾah** (disavowal) from **shirk** (associating partners) and a general judgment about a religion of shirk, without judging a specific person by name. Precisely here lies the difference between **takfīr bil-ʿumūm** (a general judgment) and **takfīr al-muʿayyan** (a judgment about a specific person).

takfir-bil-umum-400.title: 📖 ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah: The Jāhiliyyah upon misguidance
takfir-bil-umum-400.body:
🖋️ **ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah** said, in meaning, about his time before Islam:

***“I held the view that the people were upon misguidance, that they were upon nothing, and that they served the idols.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Here the state of an entire idol-worshipping society is described in general as **bāṭil** (null) and **misguidance**. That is a general classification of shirk and its people in the state of the Jāhiliyyah, not automatically a detailed individual judgment about every specific person.

takfir-bil-umum-401.title: 📖 Abū Zurʿah and Abū Ḥātim: The Jahmiyyah are Kuffār
takfir-bil-umum-401.body:
🖋️ **Abū Zurʿah ar-Rāzī and Abū Ḥātim ar-Rāzī** said in meaning:

***“The Jahmiyyah are Kuffār.”***

They explained that the **Qurʾān is the Word of Allah** and is **not created**. Whoever claims that the Qurʾān is created commits Kufr; and whoever understands this Kufr and still doubts it is judged severely.

🌙 **Conclusion:** This statement is a clear example of **Takfīr bil-ʿUmūm** concerning a doctrine and the group that follows it. At the same time the boundary remains important: the ignorant person, or one who stops because of unclarity, is taught; the judgment upon an individual remains bound to conditions and impediments.

takfir-bil-umum-402.title: 📖 Imām Mālik: Whoever says that the Qurʾān is created
takfir-bil-umum-402.body:
🖋️ It is transmitted **from Imām Mālik** that he gave a very severe general classification concerning the statement “The Qurʾān is created”:

***“The statement that the Qurʾān is created was rejected by the Imāms in general as Kufr.”***

al-Lālakāʾī places this section expressly among the transmitted Fatwā statements about the one who says: **“The Qurʾān is created.”** Mālik and further Imāms are named in it.

🌙 **Conclusion:** This is a general judgment upon a **statement of Kufr** in the ʿAqīdah: the Qurʾān is the Word of Allah and is not created. The general judgment upon the statement must still be distinguished from applying it to a specific person.

takfir-bil-umum-403.title: 📖 Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq: Separate the judgment on the state and on individuals
takfir-bil-umum-403.body:
🖋️ **Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq** distinguished between the outward state of a land and the judgment upon specific individuals.

He explained in meaning: When Shirk becomes visible in a land, forbidden things are practiced openly, and the marks of the religion are set aside, then the outward state of that land is judged severely. At the same time he made clear that there may be individuals within it about whom one does not pass a blanket inward judgment, such as the weak or those who are excused.

🌙 **Conclusion:** This statement concerns the **outward state** and the general classification of visible Shirk and of laws that contradict it. It is not a call to action and not a blanket individual Takfīr upon every person. Judgments upon individuals remain bound to conditions, impediments, and a clear establishment of proof.

takfir-bil-umum-404.title: 📖 Salmān al-Fārisī: Fiṭrah against Shirk and the search for the truth
takfir-bil-umum-404.body:
🖋️ **Salmān al-Fārisī** reported about his state before Islām:

***“The people of my village worshipped the piebald horses; I knew that they were upon nothing.”***

And when he later saw another form of worship, he said:

***“This — by Allah — is better than the religion upon which we are.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Salmān recognized, from **Fiṭrah** (natural disposition) and clear **ʿAql** (intellect), that open Shirk and a false religion are not the truth. This is a general disavowal of error and a search for Tawḥīd — yet not a named individual Takfīr upon every person.

takfir-bil-umum-405.title: 📖 Zayd ibn ʿAmr: No slaughter for idols
takfir-bil-umum-405.body:
🖋️ **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** said to the Quraysh:

***“I do not eat of what you slaughter upon your sacrificial stones; I eat only of that over which the name of Allah was mentioned.”***

He rebuked the slaughters of the Quraysh because they were done upon other than the name of Allah.

🌙 **Conclusion:** Zayd showed a clear **Barāʾah** from Shirk in worship and in slaughter. This is a general rejection of a practice of Shirk, not automatically a named individual judgment upon every specific person.

takfir-bil-umum-406.title: 📖 Zayd ibn ʿAmr: Seeking the religion of Ibrāhīm
takfir-bil-umum-406.body:
🖋️ **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** sought the true religion and asked about the Ḥanīfiyyah.

It was explained to him that the Ḥanīfiyyah is the religion of Ibrāhīm: neither Judaism nor Christianity, but **to worship Allah alone**. Thereupon Zayd said in meaning:

***“O Allah, I testify that I am upon the religion of Ibrāhīm.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** This report shows Zayd’s disavowal of the existing distorted paths and his return to the Tawḥīd of Ibrāhīm. The correct formulation here is not a direct quotation, “the people are on the wrong path,” but his clear search for the Ḥanīfiyyah and his binding himself to it.

takfir-bil-umum-407.title: 📖 Zayd ibn ʿAmr: None of you is upon the religion of Ibrāhīm
takfir-bil-umum-407.body:
🖋️ **Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr** reported that Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl stood with his back to the Kaʿbah and said:

***“O people of Quraysh! By Allah, none of you is upon the religion of Ibrāhīm except me.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** This statement is a strong example of **Takfīr bil-ʿUmūm**: Zayd judges the general religious state of the Quraysh, because they had left the religion of Ibrāhīm. This is a general judgment upon the state of Shirk, not automatically an individual judgment, with all its conditions, upon every specific person.

takfir-bil-umum-408.title: 📖 Mujāhid: Ibrāhīm was a believer alone
takfir-bil-umum-408.body:
🖋️ **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** said about Allah’s statement that Ibrāhīm was an Ummah:

***“He was a believer alone, while the people at that time were all Kuffār.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The truth of **Tawḥīd** does not depend on the majority. Ibrāhīm was alone upon Īmān and Tawḥīd, while his surroundings were in Kufr and Shirk. This is a general judgment upon the religious state of a time, not the thoughtless application to specific individuals without conditions.

tarbiyah-das-kind-wird-auf-reinheit-gebo.title: 📖 Tarbiyah: The child is born upon purity
tarbiyah-das-kind-wird-auf-reinheit-gebo.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Every newborn is born upon the Fiṭrah; then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a fire-worshipper.’”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Upbringing forms. Therefore Tarbiyah is not only provision for the body, but protection of the Fiṭrah and the building of the Dīn.

tarbiyah-erziehung-beginnt-mit-sanftmut-.title: 📖 Tarbiyah: Upbringing begins with gentleness
tarbiyah-erziehung-beginnt-mit-sanftmut-.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Gentleness is in nothing except that it beautifies it; and it is removed from nothing except that it disfigures it.’”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Severity without wisdom breaks hearts. Rifq (gentleness) makes upbringing able to bear its load and opens the way to acceptance.

tarbiyah-jeder-traegt-verantwortung-254.title: 📖 Tarbiyah: Everyone bears responsibility
tarbiyah-jeder-traegt-verantwortung-254.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.’”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tarbiyah is an Amānah (a trust). Parents, teachers, and those in charge will be asked about what was entrusted to them.

tarbiyah-kinder-auf-das-gebet-hinweisen-.title: 📖 Tarbiyah: Direct the children to the prayer
tarbiyah-kinder-auf-das-gebet-hinweisen-.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Command your children to pray when they are seven years old.’”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tarbiyah needs an early habituation to obedience toward Allah. The prayer is not a side topic, but a pillar of the house.

tarbiyah-wer-nicht-barmherzig-ist-erfaeh.title: 📖 Tarbiyah: Whoever is not merciful is not shown mercy
tarbiyah-wer-nicht-barmherzig-ist-erfaeh.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Whoever is not merciful, mercy is not shown to him.’”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tarbiyah is not only instruction. It needs Raḥmah (mercy), so that the heart does not flee from the good.

tawakkul-binde-sie-und-vertraue-001.title: 📖 Tie her and trust
tawakkul-binde-sie-und-vertraue-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Tie her and trust in Allah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **Tawakkul** does not mean abandoning the means. The believer takes the permitted means and still binds his heart ***to Allah alone***.

tawakkul-frag-nur-allah-001.title: 📖 When you ask, ask Allah
tawakkul-frag-nur-allah-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said to Ibn ʿAbbās:

> ***“When you ask, ask Allah. And when you seek help, seek help from Allah.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **Tawakkul** begins where the heart releases its dependence on the creation and binds itself to **Allah**. Whoever seeks help should flee first to ***Allah***.

tawakkul-hasbunallah-001.title: 📖 Ḥasbunā Allah wa niʿma al-Wakīl
tawakkul-hasbunallah-001.body:
🖋️ **Ibn ʿAbbās** said:

> ***“Ḥasbunā Allah wa niʿma al-Wakīl was said by Ibrāhīm عليه السلام when he was cast into the fire; and Muḥammad ﷺ said it when it was said to him: The people have gathered against you.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **Tawakkul** appears when the heart does not break in distress, but binds itself to **Allah**. Whoever takes Allah as the ***best Trustee*** does not stand alone — even when the people gather against him.

tawakkul-und-nutzen-001.title: 📖 Strive for what benefits you
tawakkul-und-nutzen-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not become incapable.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** **Tawakkul** is not standing still. The believer acts, exerts himself, and at the same time seeks ***help from Allah***.

tawakkul-wie-die-voegel-001.title: 📖 Tawakkul like the birds
tawakkul-wie-die-voegel-001.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“If you were to rely upon Allah as is due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they leave in the morning hungry and return in the evening full.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** True **Tawakkul** does not mean inactivity, but ***trust in Allah together with permitted effort***. The birds do not stay sitting — they go out, and their **Rizq** comes from Allah.

tawhid-079-haqq-allah-ala-al-ibad.title: 📖 The right of Allah over the servants
tawhid-079-haqq-allah-ala-al-ibad.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The right of Allah over the servants is that they **worship Him alone** and **associate nothing with Him**.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tawḥīd does not begin with claims, but with **ʿIbādah for Allah alone**.

tawhid-080-tawhid-fuehrt-zur-jannah.title: 📖 Whoever meets Allah without Shirk
tawhid-080-tawhid-fuehrt-zur-jannah.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Whoever meets Allah without **associating anything with Him** enters Paradise; and whoever meets Him with Shirk enters the Fire.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The greatest difference at the end is **Tawḥīd or Shirk**.

tawhid-081-dua-an-andere-als-allah.title: 📖 Whoever calls upon a rival besides Allah
tawhid-081-dua-an-andere-als-allah.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Whoever dies while he **calls upon a rival besides Allah** enters the Fire.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Duʿāʾ is ʿIbādah — therefore it belongs to **Allah alone**.

tawhid-082-la-ilaha-illa-allah-um-allahs.title: 📖 Spoken while seeking the Face of Allah
tawhid-082-la-ilaha-illa-allah-um-allahs.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“No servant meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection with **Lā ilāha illa Allah**, seeking thereby **the Face of Allah**, except that Allah bars him from the Fire.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Shahādah avails with **Ikhlāṣ**, not as an empty tongue without truth.

tawhid-083-wissen-ueber-la-ilaha-illa-al.title: 📖 Dying with knowledge of Tawḥīd
tawhid-083-wissen-ueber-la-ilaha-illa-al.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Whoever dies while he **knows** that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah enters Paradise.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tawḥīd is not merely a word — it requires **knowledge, meaning, and affirmation**.

tawhid-084-das-beste-wort-der-propheten.title: 📖 The best word of the Prophets
tawhid-084-das-beste-wort-der-propheten.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“The best of what I and the Prophets before me said is: **Lā ilāha illa Allah**, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion, and to Him is due the praise.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** The message of the Prophets is one: **Allah alone**.

tawhid-085-keine-uebertreibung-beim-prop.title: 📖 No exaggeration regarding the Prophet ﷺ
tawhid-085-keine-uebertreibung-beim-prop.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians exaggerated regarding the son of Maryam. I am only His servant; so say: **the servant of Allah and His Messenger**.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Love for the Prophet ﷺ remains true when it **protects Tawḥīd**.

tawhid-086-kein-shirk-und-vergebung.title: 📖 No associating of partners, and immense forgiveness
tawhid-086-kein-shirk-und-vergebung.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“If you came to Me with an earth full of sins and then met Me without **associating anything with Me**, I would meet you with an earth full of forgiveness.”***

🌙 **Conclusion:** Tawḥīd is the greatest cause of **forgiveness**, so long as the servant avoids Shirk.

tawhid-087-dhikr-der-einzigkeit-allahs.title: 📖 The dhikr of Allah’s oneness
tawhid-087-dhikr-der-einzigkeit-allahs.body:
🖋️ **The Prophet ﷺ** said:

> ***“Whoever says one hundred times in a day: **Lā ilāha illa Allah**, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion, and to Him is due the praise — he receives immense reward and protection.”***
