Unser Herr, wen Du ins Feuer eintreten l.occasion: In fear of the reckoning and in plea for rescue
Unser Herr, wen Du ins Feuer eintreten l.meaning: Our Lord, whomever You cause to enter the Fire, him You have truly disgraced; and the wrongdoers have no helpers.

Duʿāʾ um Rettung vor Schande am Jüngsten.title: Duʿāʾ for rescue from disgrace on the Last Day
Duʿāʾ um Rettung vor Schande am Jüngsten.occasion: In fear of the reckoning and in plea for rescue
Duʿāʾ um Rettung vor Schande am Jüngsten.meaning: Our Lord, whomever You cause to enter the Fire, him You have truly disgraced; and the wrongdoers have no helpers.

Unser Herr, gib uns, was Du uns durch De.title: Duʿāʾ for the fulfillment of the promise
Unser Herr, gib uns, was Du uns durch De.occasion: A plea for Jannah, rescue and no disgrace on the Last Day
Unser Herr, gib uns, was Du uns durch De.meaning: Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break the promise.

Duʿāʾ um Erfüllung der Verheißung.title: Duʿāʾ for the fulfillment of the promise
Duʿāʾ um Erfüllung der Verheißung.occasion: A plea for Jannah, rescue and no disgrace on the Last Day
Duʿāʾ um Erfüllung der Verheißung.meaning: Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break the promise.

Unser Herr, wir haben uns selbst Unrecht.title: Duʿāʾ after wronging oneself
Unser Herr, wir haben uns selbst Unrecht.occasion: In repentance, insight and a plea for mercy
Unser Herr, wir haben uns selbst Unrecht.meaning: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.

Duʿāʾ nach eigenem Unrecht.title: Duʿāʾ after wronging oneself
Duʿāʾ nach eigenem Unrecht.occasion: In repentance, insight and a plea for mercy
Duʿāʾ nach eigenem Unrecht.meaning: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.

Unser Herr, mache uns nicht mit dem unge.title: Duʿāʾ not to be with the wrongdoers
Unser Herr, mache uns nicht mit dem unge.occasion: In fear of bad company, wrongdoing and misguidance
Unser Herr, mache uns nicht mit dem unge.meaning: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.

Duʿāʾ nicht mit den Ungerechten zu sein.title: Duʿāʾ not to be with the wrongdoers
Duʿāʾ nicht mit den Ungerechten zu sein.occasion: In fear of bad company, wrongdoing and misguidance
Duʿāʾ nicht mit den Ungerechten zu sein.meaning: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.

Mein Herr, mache mich zu einem, der das.title: Duʿāʾ for steadfast prayer
Mein Herr, mache mich zu einem, der das.occasion: For regular prayer and righteous offspring
Mein Herr, mache mich zu einem, der das.meaning: My Lord, make me one who performs the prayer, and also from my offspring. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.

Duʿāʾ um beständiges Gebet.title: Duʿāʾ for steadfast prayer
Duʿāʾ um beständiges Gebet.occasion: For regular prayer and righteous offspring
Duʿāʾ um beständiges Gebet.meaning: My Lord, make me one who performs the prayer, and also from my offspring. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.

Unser Herr, vergib mir und meinen Eltern.title: Duʿāʾ for forgiveness for oneself, one’s parents and the believers
Unser Herr, vergib mir und meinen Eltern.occasion: For forgiveness on the Day of Reckoning
Unser Herr, vergib mir und meinen Eltern.meaning: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning takes place.

Duʿāʾ um Vergebung für sich, Eltern und.title: Duʿāʾ for forgiveness for oneself, one’s parents and the believers
Duʿāʾ um Vergebung für sich, Eltern und.occasion: For forgiveness on the Day of Reckoning
Duʿāʾ um Vergebung für sich, Eltern und.meaning: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning takes place.

Auf Allah vertrauen wir. Unser Herr, mac.title: Duʿāʾ not to become a trial for the wrongdoers
Auf Allah vertrauen wir. Unser Herr, mac.occasion: In distress, oppression and trust in Allāh
Auf Allah vertrauen wir. Unser Herr, mac.meaning: In Allāh we place our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.

Duʿāʾ nicht zur Prüfung für Ungerechte z.title: Duʿāʾ not to become a trial for the wrongdoers
Duʿāʾ nicht zur Prüfung für Ungerechte z.occasion: In distress, oppression and trust in Allāh
Duʿāʾ nicht zur Prüfung für Ungerechte z.meaning: In Allāh we place our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.

Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir da.title: Duʿāʾ not to ask in ignorance
Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir da.occasion: When one asks Allāh for something whose outcome one does not know
Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir da.meaning: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You for something of which I have no knowledge. If You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.

Duʿāʾ nicht unwissend zu bitten.title: Duʿāʾ not to ask in ignorance
Duʿāʾ nicht unwissend zu bitten.occasion: When one asks Allāh for something whose outcome one does not know
Duʿāʾ nicht unwissend zu bitten.meaning: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You for something of which I have no knowledge. If You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.

Mein Herr, Du hast mir von der Herrschaf.title: Duʿāʾ of Yūsuf for a good ending
Mein Herr, Du hast mir von der Herrschaf.occasion: In gratitude, success and a plea for a good death
Mein Herr, Du hast mir von der Herrschaf.meaning: My Lord, You have given me something of sovereignty and taught me something of the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.

Duʿāʾ von Yūsuf um guten Abschluss.title: Duʿāʾ of Yūsuf for a good ending
Duʿāʾ von Yūsuf um guten Abschluss.occasion: In gratitude, success and a plea for a good death
Duʿāʾ von Yūsuf um guten Abschluss.meaning: My Lord, You have given me something of sovereignty and taught me something of the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.

Mein Herr, lass mich einen wahrhaftigen.title: Duʿāʾ for a truthful entrance and exit
Mein Herr, lass mich einen wahrhaftigen.occasion: At new paths, tasks, journeys or difficult decisions
Mein Herr, lass mich einen wahrhaftigen.meaning: My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and to go out a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a helping authority.

Duʿāʾ um ehrlichen Eintritt und Ausgang.title: Duʿāʾ for a truthful entrance and exit
Duʿāʾ um ehrlichen Eintritt und Ausgang.occasion: At new paths, tasks, journeys or difficult decisions
Duʿāʾ um ehrlichen Eintritt und Ausgang.meaning: My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and to go out a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a helping authority.

Mein Herr, weite mir meine Brust, erleic.title: Duʿāʾ of Mūsā for ease and clear speech
Mein Herr, weite mir meine Brust, erleic.occasion: Before conversations, teaching, Daʿwah, an examination or a difficult task
Mein Herr, weite mir meine Brust, erleic.meaning: My Lord, expand my breast for me, make my affair easy for me, and untie the knot from my tongue, so that they understand my words.

Duʿāʾ von Mūsā um Erleichterung und klar.title: Duʿāʾ of Mūsā for ease and clear speech
Duʿāʾ von Mūsā um Erleichterung und klar.occasion: Before conversations, teaching, Daʿwah, an examination or a difficult task
Duʿāʾ von Mūsā um Erleichterung und klar.meaning: My Lord, expand my breast for me, make my affair easy for me, and untie the knot from my tongue, so that they understand my words.

Mein Herr, lass mich nicht allein zurück.title: Duʿāʾ of Zakariyyā for offspring
Mein Herr, lass mich nicht allein zurück.occasion: When hoping for a child and asking for righteous offspring
Mein Herr, lass mich nicht allein zurück.meaning: My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors.

Duʿāʾ von Zakariyyā um Nachkommen.title: Duʿāʾ of Zakariyyā for offspring
Duʿāʾ von Zakariyyā um Nachkommen.occasion: When hoping for a child and asking for righteous offspring
Duʿāʾ von Zakariyyā um Nachkommen.meaning: My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors.

Unser Herr, vergib mir, meinen Eltern un.title: Seeking forgiveness for parents and believers
Unser Herr, vergib mir, meinen Eltern un.occasion: For oneself, one's parents and all believers
Unser Herr, vergib mir, meinen Eltern un.meaning: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will take place.

Bitte um Vergebung für Eltern und Gläubi.title: Seeking forgiveness for parents and believers
Bitte um Vergebung für Eltern und Gläubi.occasion: For oneself, one's parents and all believers
Bitte um Vergebung für Eltern und Gläubi.meaning: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will take place.

Unser Herr, schenke uns Barmherzigkeit v.title: Seeking mercy and a right way
Unser Herr, schenke uns Barmherzigkeit v.occasion: In distress, difficult decisions and the search for a way out
Unser Herr, schenke uns Barmherzigkeit v.meaning: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us a right way in our affair.

Bitte um Barmherzigkeit und einen rechte.title: Seeking mercy and a right way
Bitte um Barmherzigkeit und einen rechte.occasion: In distress, difficult decisions and the search for a way out
Bitte um Barmherzigkeit und einen rechte.meaning: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us a right way in our affair.

Mein Herr, mehre mich an Wissen..title: Seeking an increase in knowledge
Mein Herr, mehre mich an Wissen..meaning: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

Bitte um Mehrung des Wissens.title: Seeking an increase in knowledge
Bitte um Mehrung des Wissens.meaning: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vo.title: Protection from the whispers of the Shayāṭīn
Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vo.occasion: At times of whispers, fear and inner unrest
Mein Herr, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vo.meaning: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the Shayāṭīn, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their being present with me.

Schutz vor den Einflüsterungen der Shayā.title: Protection from the whispers of the Shayāṭīn
Schutz vor den Einflüsterungen der Shayā.occasion: At times of whispers, fear and inner unrest
Schutz vor den Einflüsterungen der Shayā.meaning: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the Shayāṭīn, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their being present with me.

Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Ehepa.title: Supplication for a righteous family
Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Ehepa.occasion: For spouses, children and righteous offspring
Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Ehepa.meaning: Our Lord, grant us joy of the eyes from our spouses and offspring, and make us examples for the God-fearing.

Bitte um rechtschaffene Familie.title: Supplication for a righteous family
Bitte um rechtschaffene Familie.occasion: For spouses, children and righteous offspring
Bitte um rechtschaffene Familie.meaning: Our Lord, grant us joy of the eyes from our spouses and offspring, and make us examples for the God-fearing.

O Allah, hilf mir, Deiner zu gedenken, D.title: Help in remembrance and good worship
O Allah, hilf mir, Deiner zu gedenken, D.occasion: At the end of the prayer and in general for good worship
O Allah, hilf mir, Deiner zu gedenken, D.meaning: O Allāh, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You in the best way.

Hilfe beim Gedenken und guten Gottesdien.title: Help in remembrance and good worship
Hilfe beim Gedenken und guten Gottesdien.occasion: At the end of the prayer and in general for good worship
Hilfe beim Gedenken und guten Gottesdien.meaning: O Allāh, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You in the best way.

O Allah, ich habe mir selbst viel Unrech.title: Comprehensive supplication for forgiveness
O Allah, ich habe mir selbst viel Unrech.occasion: In the prayer and in sincere repentance
O Allah, ich habe mir selbst viel Unrech.meaning: O Allāh, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with a forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. You are indeed the All-Forgiving, the Merciful.

Umfassende Bitte um Vergebung.title: Comprehensive supplication for forgiveness
Umfassende Bitte um Vergebung.occasion: In the prayer and in sincere repentance
Umfassende Bitte um Vergebung.meaning: O Allāh, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with a forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. You are indeed the All-Forgiving, the Merciful.

O Allah, Lenker der Herzen, richte unser.title: Supplication to direct the hearts toward obedience
O Allah, Lenker der Herzen, richte unser.occasion: For steadfastness and obedience to Allāh
O Allah, Lenker der Herzen, richte unser.meaning: O Allāh, Turner of hearts, direct our hearts toward obedience to You.

Bitte um Ausrichtung der Herzen auf Geho.title: Supplication to direct the hearts toward obedience
Bitte um Ausrichtung der Herzen auf Geho.occasion: For steadfastness and obedience to Allāh
Bitte um Ausrichtung der Herzen auf Geho.meaning: O Allāh, Turner of hearts, direct our hearts toward obedience to You.

O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.title: Protection from the evil of one's own deeds
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of what I have not yet done.

Schutz vor dem Übel eigener Taten.title: Protection from the evil of one's own deeds
Schutz vor dem Übel eigener Taten.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of what I have not yet done.

Mein Herr, vergib mir und nimm meine Reu.title: A short, frequent plea for forgiveness
Mein Herr, vergib mir und nimm meine Reu.occasion: For frequent Istighfār in daily life
Mein Herr, vergib mir und nimm meine Reu.meaning: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. You are indeed the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.

Kurze häufige Bitte um Vergebung.title: A short, frequent plea for forgiveness
Kurze häufige Bitte um Vergebung.occasion: For frequent Istighfār in daily life
Kurze häufige Bitte um Vergebung.meaning: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. You are indeed the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.

O Allah, leite mich recht und lasse mich.title: Seeking right guidance and right action
O Allah, leite mich recht und lasse mich.meaning: O Allāh, guide me aright and make me act rightly.

Bitte um Rechtleitung und richtiges Hand.title: Seeking right guidance and right action
Bitte um Rechtleitung und richtiges Hand.meaning: O Allāh, guide me aright and make me act rightly.

O Allah, Du bist mein Herr. Niemand hat.title: Sayyid al-Istighfār
O Allah, Du bist mein Herr. Niemand hat.occasion: To be said in the morning and evening with certainty
O Allah, Du bist mein Herr. Niemand hat.meaning: O Allāh, You are my Lord. None has the right to be worshipped except You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I confess my sin. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.

Sayyid al-Istighfār.title: Sayyid al-Istighfār
Sayyid al-Istighfār.occasion: To be said in the morning and evening with certainty
Sayyid al-Istighfār.meaning: O Allāh, You are my Lord. None has the right to be worshipped except You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I confess my sin. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.

O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.title: Protection from blameworthy character and conduct
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.occasion: For good character and protection from bad inclinations
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from blameworthy character, blameworthy deeds and blameworthy inclinations.

Schutz vor verwerflichem Charakter und H.title: Protection from blameworthy character and conduct
Schutz vor verwerflichem Charakter und H.occasion: For good character and protection from bad inclinations
Schutz vor verwerflichem Charakter und H.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from blameworthy character, blameworthy deeds and blameworthy inclinations.

O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.title: Protection from Kufr, poverty and the punishment of the grave
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.occasion: At the end of the prayer and in the morning and evening
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from Kufr, poverty and the punishment of the grave.

Schutz vor Kufr, Armut und Grabstrafe.title: Protection from Kufr, poverty and the punishment of the grave
Schutz vor Kufr, Armut und Grabstrafe.occasion: At the end of the prayer and in the morning and evening
Schutz vor Kufr, Armut und Grabstrafe.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from Kufr, poverty and the punishment of the grave.

O Allah, schenke mir den Märtyrertod auf.title: Duʿāʾ of ʿUmar for Shahādah
O Allah, schenke mir den Märtyrertod auf.occasion: A plea for a good death and Shahādah
O Allah, schenke mir den Märtyrertod auf.meaning: O Allāh, grant me martyrdom on Your path and let my death be in the city of Your Messenger ﷺ.

Duʿāʾ von ʿUmar um Shahādah.title: Duʿāʾ of ʿUmar for Shahādah
Duʿāʾ von ʿUmar um Shahādah.occasion: A plea for a good death and Shahādah
Duʿāʾ von ʿUmar um Shahādah.meaning: O Allāh, grant me martyrdom on Your path and let my death be in the city of Your Messenger ﷺ.

O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.title: Protection from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave and the great trials
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.occasion: After the final Tašahhud and before the Taslīm
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Dir vor.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trial of life and of death, and from the evil of the trial of the false Messiah ad-Dajjāl.

Schutz vor Höllenstrafe, Grabstrafe und.title: Protection from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave and the great trials
Schutz vor Höllenstrafe, Grabstrafe und.occasion: After the final Tašahhud and before the Taslīm
Schutz vor Höllenstrafe, Grabstrafe und.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trial of life and of death, and from the evil of the trial of the false Messiah ad-Dajjāl.

O Allah, vergib mir alle meine Sünden: i.title: Comprehensive plea for forgiveness of all sins
O Allah, vergib mir alle meine Sünden: i.meaning: O Allāh, forgive me all my sins: the small and the great, the first and the last, and the public and the hidden.

Umfassende Bitte um Vergebung aller Sünd.title: Comprehensive plea for forgiveness of all sins
Umfassende Bitte um Vergebung aller Sünd.meaning: O Allāh, forgive me all my sins: the small and the great, the first and the last, and the public and the hidden.

O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Deinem W.title: Seeking refuge in Allāh's pleasure from His wrath
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Deinem W.occasion: In Suǧūd; also connected with the Witr in authentic reports
O Allah, ich suche Zuflucht bei Deinem W.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath and in Your sparing me from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot fully enumerate praise of You. You are as You have praised Yourself.

Zuflucht bei Allahs Wohlgefallen vor Sei.title: Seeking refuge in Allāh's pleasure from His wrath
Zuflucht bei Allahs Wohlgefallen vor Sei.occasion: In Suǧūd; also connected with the Witr in authentic reports
Zuflucht bei Allahs Wohlgefallen vor Sei.meaning: O Allāh, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath and in Your sparing me from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot fully enumerate praise of You. You are as You have praised Yourself.

O Allah, wasche meine Sünden mit Schnee-.title: Supplication for purification from all sins
O Allah, wasche meine Sünden mit Schnee-.occasion: As a comprehensive plea for forgiveness and purification
O Allah, wasche meine Sünden mit Schnee-.meaning: O Allāh, wash away my sins with snow-water and hail-water. Purify my heart from sins as You purify the white garment from dirt, and distance me from my sins as You have distanced the east from the west.

Bitte um Reinigung von allen Sünden.title: Supplication for purification from all sins
Bitte um Reinigung von allen Sünden.occasion: As a comprehensive plea for forgiveness and purification
Bitte um Reinigung von allen Sünden.meaning: O Allāh, wash away my sins with snow-water and hail-water. Purify my heart from sins as You purify the white garment from dirt, and distance me from my sins as You have distanced the east from the west.

O Allah, Herr von Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl und Is.title: Seeking guidance amid differences of opinion
O Allah, Herr von Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl und Is.occasion: As the opening supplication of the night prayer
O Allah, Herr von Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl und Is.meaning: O Allāh, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen. You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in that over which there is disagreement. You guide whom You will to a straight path.

Bitte um Rechtleitung bei Meinungsversch.title: Seeking guidance amid differences of opinion
Bitte um Rechtleitung bei Meinungsversch.occasion: As the opening supplication of the night prayer
Bitte um Rechtleitung bei Meinungsversch.meaning: O Allāh, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen. You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in that over which there is disagreement. You guide whom You will to a straight path.

O Allah, Dir habe ich mich ergeben, an D.title: Duʿāʾ of complete submission and trust
O Allah, Dir habe ich mich ergeben, an D.occasion: As a comprehensive Duʿāʾ for submission, Tawakkul and protection from being led astray
O Allah, Dir habe ich mich ergeben, an D.meaning: O Allāh, to You I have submitted, in You I believe, upon You I rely and to You I turn in repentance. With Your help I confront the opponent. O Allāh, I seek refuge in Your might — none has the right to be worshipped except You — from Your letting me go astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while the Jinn and human beings die.

Duʿāʾ der vollständigen Hingabe und des.title: Duʿāʾ of complete submission and trust
Duʿāʾ der vollständigen Hingabe und des.occasion: As a comprehensive Duʿāʾ for submission, Tawakkul and protection from being led astray
Duʿāʾ der vollständigen Hingabe und des.meaning: O Allāh, to You I have submitted, in You I believe, upon You I rely and to You I turn in repentance. With Your help I confront the opponent. O Allāh, I seek refuge in Your might — none has the right to be worshipped except You — from Your letting me go astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while the Jinn and human beings die.

O Allah, nichts ist leicht außer dem, wa.title: Supplication for ease in a difficult matter
O Allah, nichts ist leicht außer dem, wa.occasion: In difficult tasks, trials and burdensome matters
O Allah, nichts ist leicht außer dem, wa.meaning: O Allāh, nothing is easy except what You have made easy. And You make the difficult easy when You will.

Bitte um Erleichterung einer schwierigen.title: Supplication for ease in a difficult matter
Bitte um Erleichterung einer schwierigen.occasion: In difficult tasks, trials and burdensome matters
Bitte um Erleichterung einer schwierigen.meaning: O Allāh, nothing is easy except what You have made easy. And You make the difficult easy when You will.

Niemand hat das Recht angebetet zu werde.title: Duʿāʾ of Yūnus in the darkness
Niemand hat das Recht angebetet zu werde.occasion: In distress, constriction, a sense of guilt, and a severe situation
Niemand hat das Recht angebetet zu werde.meaning: None has the right to be worshipped except You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.

Duʿāʾ von Yūnus in der Dunkelheit.title: Duʿāʾ of Yūnus in the darkness
Duʿāʾ von Yūnus in der Dunkelheit.occasion: In distress, constriction, a sense of guilt, and a severe situation
Duʿāʾ von Yūnus in der Dunkelheit.meaning: None has the right to be worshipped except You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.

Mein Herr, lass mich an einem gesegneten.title: Duʿāʾ for a blessed arrival
Mein Herr, lass mich an einem gesegneten.occasion: Upon arrival, lodging, moving, or travel
Mein Herr, lass mich an einem gesegneten.meaning: My Lord, let me arrive at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who grant arrival.

Duʿāʾ für eine gesegnete Ankunft.title: Duʿāʾ for a blessed arrival
Duʿāʾ für eine gesegnete Ankunft.occasion: Upon arrival, lodging, moving, or travel
Duʿāʾ für eine gesegnete Ankunft.meaning: My Lord, let me arrive at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who grant arrival.

Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Gatti.title: Duʿāʾ for joy through the family
Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Gatti.occasion: For marriage, children, and a righteous family
Unser Herr, schenke uns an unseren Gatti.meaning: Our Lord, grant us from our wives and our offspring joy for the eyes, and make us a model for the God-fearing.

Duʿāʾ um Freude durch Familie.title: Duʿāʾ for joy through the family
Duʿāʾ um Freude durch Familie.occasion: For marriage, children, and a righteous family
Duʿāʾ um Freude durch Familie.meaning: Our Lord, grant us from our wives and our offspring joy for the eyes, and make us a model for the God-fearing.

quiz-307.explanation: The Ḥadīth gathers a great part of the Dīn in Naṣīḥah.
answers: That sincerity, honest counsel, and loyalty to the Dīn belong to its great pillars.
That the Dīn consists only of feelings without obligation.
That counsel in the Dīn is superfluous.
That sincerity counts only in worldly matters.

quiz-308.question: For whom is sincerity expressly named in the Ḥadīth about Naṣīḥah?
quiz-308.explanation: The Ḥadīth expressly names these five areas as the recipients of Naṣīḥah.
answers: For الله, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims, and their general body.
Only for close friends.
Only for scholars and for no one else.
Only for rulers, not for the general body.

quiz-309.question: Which methodological teaching does the Ḥadīth “The permitted is clear, and the forbidden is clear, and between them lie doubtful matters” contain?
quiz-309.explanation: The Ḥadīth teaches caution in the Dīn and the avoidance of doubtful matters.
answers: That one avoids what is doubtful in order to protect one’s Dīn and one’s honor.
That doubtful things are without further ado unproblematic.
That only what is expressly forbidden is to be avoided, even when strong doubts exist.
That caution in the Dīn is always exaggerated.

quiz-310.question: Which overall structure of Islam is presented in the Ḥadīth “Islam was built upon five”?
quiz-310.explanation: The Ḥadīth names the five well-known pillars of Islam.
answers: That Islam rests upon five fundamental pillars.
That Islam has no fixed foundational pillars.
That only faith in the heart counts and the outward duties fall away.
That Islam consists solely of voluntary deeds.

quiz-311.question: How is Iḥsān defined in the Ḥadīth of Jibrīl?
quiz-311.explanation: The Ḥadīth of Jibrīl gives this immense definition of Iḥsān.
answers: That you worship الله as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He sees you.
That Iḥsān means only good manners without worship.
That Iḥsān is a voluntary idea without relation to worship.
That Iḥsān applies only to prophets.

quiz-312.question: Which foundation of faith is expressly mentioned in the Ḥadīth of Jibrīl among the pillars of Īmān?
quiz-312.explanation: The Ḥadīth of Jibrīl counts belief in al-Qadar among the pillars of Īmān.
answers: Belief in Allah’s predestination, the good of it and the bad of it.
That Qadar plays no role in Īmān.
That Īmān consists only of outward actions.
That belief in the angels is voluntary.

quiz-313.question: Which statement about Īmān becomes clear in the Ḥadīth “Īmān has seventy and some branches”?
quiz-313.explanation: The Ḥadīth mentions various branches of Īmān, such as uttering the Schahādah and removing what is harmful from the path.
answers: That Īmān consists of various branches, among them statements, actions, and inner deeds.
That Īmān is only knowledge without actions.
That Īmān consists only of love and has no outward consequences.
That Īmān cannot increase or decrease.

quiz-314.question: Which quality of a Muslim is named in the Ḥadīth “The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe”?
quiz-314.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the great importance of Adab, the tongue, and the protection of other Muslims.
answers: That he does not harm other Muslims with tongue or hand.
That strength in the Dīn is proven by coarse speech.
That words carry no responsibility.
That only bodily harm counts, not verbal harm.

quiz-315.question: Which attitude of the heart is required in the Ḥadīth “None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself”?
quiz-315.explanation: The Ḥadīth teaches purity of the heart and love of the good for others.
answers: Sincere love of the good for the Muslim brother.
Only indifference toward other Muslims.
That one seeks only one’s own benefit.
That Īmān is complete without conduct toward others.

quiz-316.question: Which rule of the tongue becomes clear in the Ḥadīth “Whoever believes in الله and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent”?
quiz-316.explanation: The Ḥadīth links Īmān with controlled and beneficial speech.
answers: That a believer either speaks good or remains silent.
That every kind of speech is better than silence.
That bad speech is unproblematic as long as one appears convinced.
That control of the tongue applies only to scholars.

quiz-317.question: Which excellence is mentioned in the Ḥadīth “The best among you are those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it”?
quiz-317.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the high standing of learning and teaching the Qurʾān.
answers: That learning and teaching the Qurʾān belong to the best deeds.
That knowledge of the Qurʾān should remain only private.
That teaching the Qurʾān has no special standing.
That only recitation without understanding counts.

quiz-318.question: Which great excellence is mentioned in the Ḥadīth “Whomever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding in the Dīn”?
quiz-318.explanation: The Ḥadīth names understanding of the Dīn as a sign of Allah’s good for a person.
answers: That deep understanding in the Dīn is a sign of Allah’s good for a servant.
That Fiqh in the Dīn is only optional extra knowledge.
That understanding in the Dīn is without benefit.
That wealth is a greater sign of good than Fiqh.

quiz-319.question: Which basic rule about knowledge becomes clear in the famous statement of Ibn Sīrīn: “This knowledge is Dīn, so look from whom you take your Dīn”?
quiz-319.explanation: Ibn Sīrīn made clear that knowledge must not be taken lightly, because it is Dīn.
answers: That in religious knowledge one must carefully heed the source and the teacher.
That it is indifferent from whom one takes the Dīn.
That knowledge may be learned only from books without scholars.
That false sources in the Dīn cause no harm.

quiz-320.question: Which development does Ibn Sīrīn describe concerning the time before and after the Fitnah in dealing with the Isnād?
quiz-320.explanation: Ibn Sīrīn described that after the appearance of the Fitnah people paid closer attention to the transmitters.
answers: Before, one did not ask about the Isnād; after the Fitnah one began to examine the transmitters.
After the Fitnah the Isnād became meaningless.
Before the Fitnah the Isnād was stricter than afterward.
One generally stopped asking about transmitters.

quiz-321.question: Which foundation does the well-known statement of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه convey: “Follow and do not invent anew, for you have been given sufficiency”?
quiz-321.explanation: The statement teaches holding to the transmitted Sunnah and avoiding Bidʿah.
answers: That following the transmitted guidance suffices and religious innovation is to be avoided.
That everyone may invent new paths in the religion.
That the statement of the Salaf has no methodological significance.
That the Dīn is in principle open to new forms of worship.

quiz-322.question: Which methodological rule is understood from the well-known statement of al-Awzāʿī: “Hold yourself patiently to the Sunnah and stop where the people stopped”?
quiz-322.explanation: Al-Awzāʿī emphasized holding to the Sunnah and stopping at that upon which the early righteous stood.
answers: That one holds to the Sunnah and does not go beyond the path of the Salaf.
That later opinions are in principle better than those of the Salaf.
That patience upon the Sunnah is not necessary.
That every new debate automatically brings guidance.

quiz-323.question: Which foundation does Imām Aḥmad name at the beginning of “Uṣūl as-Sunnah”?
quiz-323.explanation: Imām Aḥmad made holding to the path of the Ṣaḥābah a foundational basis of the Sunnah.
answers: Holding to that upon which the Companions of the Messenger ﷺ were.
Rebuilding the religion according to mere reason.
Viewing the practice of the Ṣaḥābah only historically.
Making no distinction between Sunnah and Bidʿah.

quiz-324.question: What meaning does the well-known statement of Imām Mālik have: “The latter part of this Ummah will not be set right by anything other than that by which its first part was set right”?
quiz-324.explanation: The statement emphasizes that true reform occurs only through the foundations upon which the first righteous generations were.
answers: That the guidance of the later Ummah remains bound to the same foundations of Qurʾān and Sunnah as with the first ones.
That every later time needs its own new religion.
That the early generations have only historical significance.
That reform arises above all through cultural innovations.

quiz-325.question: Which condition for the validity of the prayer becomes clear from the Ḥadīth “Allah does not accept the prayer without purification”?
quiz-325.explanation: The Ḥadīth clearly shows that purification is a condition for the acceptance of the prayer.
answers: That Ṭahārah is a prerequisite for the validity of the prayer.
That the prayer is valid even without purity.
That purification applies only to the Friday prayer.
That inner purity alone replaces outward Ṭahārah.

quiz-351.question: Which excellence is mentioned in the Ḥadīth about the one who takes a path in order to seek knowledge?
quiz-351.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the great standing of seeking Islamic knowledge.
answers: الله thereby makes a path to Paradise easy for him.
Knowledge has no special reward.
Knowledge is obligatory only for scholars and of no benefit to others.
The path of knowledge is lesser than mere opinion.

quiz-352.question: How does the Ḥadīth describe that knowledge is taken away at the end?
quiz-352.explanation: The Ḥadīth warns that with the death of the scholars knowledge disappears and the ignorant speak without knowledge.
answers: By the scholars dying until ignorant leaders remain.
By books suddenly disappearing.
By every person automatically becoming a scholar.
By knowledge growing stronger without a teacher and without understanding.

quiz-353.question: Which responsibility becomes clear in the Ḥadīth “Convey from me, even if it is only one verse”?
quiz-353.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the passing on of knowledge, but within the duty of truthfulness and accuracy.
answers: Knowledge from the Prophet ﷺ is to be passed on reliably.
Anyone may attribute whatever statements he wishes to the Prophet ﷺ.
Only great scholars may mention anything from Islam at all.
Transmission needs no accuracy.

quiz-354.question: Which severe warning does the Ḥadīth contain about someone who deliberately lies about the Prophet ﷺ?
quiz-354.explanation: The Ḥadīth is one of the strongest warnings against invented or deliberately false reports.
answers: He is to take his place in the Fire.
It is only a minor sin without a special warning.
It is permissible if the statement sounds good.
It is forbidden only when many people are listening.

quiz-355.question: Which rule becomes clear from the statement that it is enough of a lie for a person to relate everything he hears?
quiz-355.explanation: The statement teaches caution when passing on news and reports.
answers: Not every statement one hears may be passed on without examination.
Everything heard is automatically true.
Passing something on without examination is a virtue.
Whoever relates a great deal is automatically more accurate.

quiz-356.question: What is the meaning of the well-known statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak: “The Isnād belongs to the Dīn”?
quiz-356.explanation: Ibn al-Mubārak made clear that the Isnād is an essential means of preserving the Dīn.
answers: That the chain of transmission is a protection for the religion.
That chains of sources play no role in Islam.
That anyone may relate whatever he wishes without examination.
That the Dīn consists only of opinions without transmission.

quiz-357.question: What did Ibn al-Mubārak mean by the statement that without an Isnād anyone could say what he wanted?
quiz-357.explanation: The statement shows the protective function of the Isnād against lies, errors, and unsubstantiated claims.
answers: That the Isnād protects the religion from baseless claims.
That it is better to work without chains of transmission.
That every statement is accepted automatically.
That examining the transmitters is an innovation.

quiz-358.question: Which rule is understood from the Ḥadīth about the judge who performs ijtihād and is right or wrong?
quiz-358.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the standing of qualified ijtihād and distinguishes it from speaking in ignorance.
answers: The qualified judge is rewarded for his ijtihād, even if he errs in an honest effort.
Any ignorant person may issue legal rulings without knowledge.
An error in judgment is always the same as a deliberate lie.
Ijtihād requires no qualification.

quiz-359.question: Which rule is understood from the Ḥadīth about someone who forgets while fasting and eats or drinks?
quiz-359.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows a facilitation in the case of forgetfulness during the fast.
answers: He completes his fast, for الله has fed him and given him drink.
His fast is invalid in every case.
He must repeat the entire month.
He may afterwards continue eating deliberately.

quiz-360.question: Which excellence of the Suḥūr is mentioned in the Ḥadīth?
quiz-360.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the Sunnah and the blessing of the Suḥūr.
answers: There is blessing in the Suḥūr.
The Suḥūr is forbidden.
The Suḥūr is only a cultural custom.
The Suḥūr has no connection to fasting.

quiz-361.question: Which Sunnah is understood from the Ḥadīth that the people remain upon good so long as they hasten the breaking of the fast?
quiz-361.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the Sunnah of breaking the fast promptly once its time has entered.
answers: Breaking the fast at the proper time, without unnecessary delay.
Deliberately delaying the Iftār until late at night.
Omitting the Iftār.
Breaking the fast before sunset.

quiz-362.question: Which basis is understood from the Ḥadīth “Fast when you see it, and break the fast when you see it”?
quiz-362.explanation: The Ḥadīth is a basis for determining Ramaḍān and its end.
answers: The beginning and the end of the month are tied to the sighting of the Hilāl.
Ramaḍān begins according to personal feeling.
Ramaḍān always begins on some arbitrary fixed weekday.
The sighting of the moon has no significance in Fiqh.

quiz-363.question: Which rule is understood from the Ḥadīth about the two parties to a sale, who have an option so long as they have not separated?
quiz-363.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows that trade in Islam is regulated by clear rights and fairness.
answers: In trade there are regulated rights and clarity between buyer and seller.
Contracts of sale need no rules.
The buyer never has a right.
The seller may exploit every ambiguity.

quiz-364.question: Which rule is understood from the Ḥadīth “Whoever deceives us is not of us”?
quiz-364.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the severe warning against fraud and deception.
answers: Deception is severely forbidden in Islam.
Deception is permissible if it brings profit.
Deception is forbidden only toward Muslims.
Deception is a normal strategy in trade.

quiz-365.question: Which fiqh basis becomes clear from the Ḥadīths about gold for gold, silver for silver, and similar goods of exchange?
quiz-365.explanation: The Ribā Ḥadīths form a major basis in the Fiqh of sales.
answers: That the rules of Ribā, for certain goods of exchange, require equality and direct handover.
That Ribā plays no role in trade.
That gold and silver may always be exchanged unequally at will.
That the rules of trade are only cultural recommendations.

quiz-366.question: Which rule is understood from the Ḥadīth that there is no vow in disobedience toward الله?
quiz-366.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows that a vow may not be used to make a sin binding.
answers: A vow that contains disobedience is not fulfilled as an act of obedience.
Every vow is permissible, even if it includes a sin.
Vows have no rules in Islam.
Disobedience becomes automatically permissible by means of a vow.

quiz-367.question: Which standing of modesty is mentioned in the Ḥadīth?
quiz-367.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows that ḥayāʾ is a religious quality and part of Īmān.
answers: Modesty is a branch of Īmān.
Modesty has nothing to do with Īmān.
Modesty is always weakness.
Modesty applies only in trade.

quiz-368.question: Which effect of gentleness is mentioned in the Ḥadīth?
quiz-368.explanation: The Ḥadīth teaches the great effect of Rifq in dealing with people.
answers: Gentleness adorns a matter, and its absence disfigures it.
Harshness is always more beautiful than gentleness.
Gentleness is permissible only with families.
Gentleness has no place in Daʿwah and upbringing.

quiz-369.question: Which rule becomes clear in the Ḥadīth “Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy”?
quiz-369.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the central place of Raḥmah in the conduct of the Muslim.
answers: Mercy toward creatures is an important quality in the Dīn.
Harshness is always the highest form of the Dīn.
Mercy applies only toward close relatives.
Mercy is not an Islamic subject.

quiz-370.question: How is true strength described in the Ḥadīth about the strong person?
quiz-370.explanation: The Ḥadīth corrects the understanding of strength and connects it with self-control.
answers: As mastery of one’s own soul at the time of anger.
As victory in every dispute.
As a loud and harsh manner.
As the ability to humiliate others.

quiz-371.question: Which short admonition did the Prophet ﷺ repeat to a man who asked him for advice?
quiz-371.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the danger of anger and the importance of self-control.
answers: Do not become angry.
Seek dispute.
Always answer at once with harshness.
Let anger determine your judgment.

quiz-372.question: Which connection does the Ḥadīth draw between belief in الله and the Last Day and conduct toward the neighbor?
quiz-372.explanation: The Ḥadīth connects Īmān with good conduct toward neighbors.
answers: Whoever believes in الله and the Last Day should honor his neighbor.
The rights of the neighbor have no connection to faith.
The neighbor has rights only if he is a relative.
Good conduct applies only inside the mosque.

quiz-373.question: Which action is connected, in the same Ḥadīth, with belief in الله and the Last Day?
quiz-373.explanation: The Ḥadīth names hospitality as a sign of good Islamic conduct.
answers: Honoring the guest.
Despising the guest.
Abandoning hospitality completely.
Treating well only wealthy guests.

quiz-374.question: Which teaching does the Ḥadīth about the strong believer and the weak believer contain?
quiz-374.explanation: The Ḥadīth connects strength with benefit, striving, and trust in الله, not with arrogance.
answers: The strong believer is better and more beloved to الله, and in both there is good.
Only physical strength counts in the Dīn.
The weak believer has no good in him at all.
The believer should not take up beneficial means.

quiz-375.question: Which rule of action follows in the Ḥadīth about the strong believer after the mention of his excellence?
quiz-375.explanation: The Ḥadīth connects taking beneficial means with Tawakkul and steadfastness.
answers: Strive for what benefits you, seek help from الله, and do not grow weak.
Abandon all means.
Rely only on your own strength.
Give up beneficial aims as soon as they become difficult.

quiz-376.question: Which false attitude does the Ḥadīth correct when something difficult has occurred?
quiz-376.explanation: The Ḥadīth teaches contentment with the decree of الله after a matter has occurred and warns against harmful brooding.
answers: The constant “If only...” in a way that opens the way for Shayṭān.
Taking hold of causes before the action.
Trust in الله.
Learning from mistakes.

quiz-377.question: Which duty of faith is named in the Ḥadīth that no one believes completely until the Prophet ﷺ is more beloved to him than father, child, and all people?
quiz-377.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the central place of love for the Prophet ﷺ in Īmān.
answers: The special love for the Prophet ﷺ above all people.
That love for the Prophet ﷺ is only a cultural matter.
That one regards the Prophet ﷺ only like any other teacher.
That love plays no role in Īmān.

quiz-378.question: Which foundation belongs to the three things by which, in the Ḥadīth, one finds the sweetness of Īmān?
quiz-378.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the connection between love, Īmān, and the inner sweetness of faith.
answers: That الله and His Messenger ﷺ are more beloved to one than everything else.
That worldly rank is more beloved to one than the Dīn.
That one knows the Dīn only outwardly.
That love for الله plays no role.

quiz-379.question: Which further quality belongs, in the Ḥadīth, to the sweetness of Īmān?
quiz-379.explanation: The Ḥadīth teaches that love for الله is an important quality of Īmān.
answers: That one loves a person only for الله.
That love in the Dīn arises only according to benefit.
That one loves people only according to lineage.
That love and hate have nothing to do with Īmān.

quiz-380.question: Which attitude toward falling back into Kufr is mentioned in the Ḥadīth about the sweetness of Īmān?
quiz-380.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows aversion to Kufr as part of the sweetness and firmness of Īmān.
answers: One hates to return to Kufr as one hates to be thrown into the Fire.
One regards Kufr and Īmān as equal.
One sees no difference between guidance and misguidance.
One makes Īmān depend only on culture.

quiz-381.question: Which attitude toward the Companions رضي الله عنهم is required in the Ḥadīth “Do not revile my Companions”?
quiz-381.explanation: The Ḥadīth protects the standing of the Ṣaḥābah and warns against reviling them.
answers: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ must not be reviled.
The Companions are to be treated like ordinary political figures.
The merit of the Ṣaḥābah is meaningless.
Reviling the Ṣaḥābah belongs to the critique of knowledge.

quiz-382.question: Which generation is named first in the Ḥadīth “The best people are my generation”?
quiz-382.explanation: The Ḥadīth establishes the special merit of the first generation.
answers: The generation of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions.
A later generation without connection to the Sunnah.
Only people of a particular lineage.
All generations without distinction.

quiz-383.question: Which methodological rule is contained in the well-known statement of Imām Mālik that everyone may be taken from and rejected in his statement — except the inhabitant of this grave, that is, the Prophet ﷺ?
quiz-383.explanation: The statement shows respect for the scholars, and also the absolute precedence of the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.
answers: Only the Prophet ﷺ is absolutely authoritative in his religious statement.
Every scholar is infallible.
One follows scholars even against a clear Ḥadīth.
The Sunnah is less important than later opinions.

quiz-384.question: Which attitude of the Salaf becomes clear from the statements of Imām Aḥmad about holding fast to the Āthār and the Sunnah?
quiz-384.explanation: Imām Aḥmad was known for his strong adherence to the Sunnah and the Āthār.
answers: The Sunnah and the Āthār are taken as the foundation, not mere opinion.
Mere opinion stands above the Āthār.
The Āthār of the early Muslims are without benefit.
The Dīn is built independently of transmission.

quiz-385.question: Which basic attitude of the early scholars appears in the reports of al-Lālikāʾī about holding fast to the Sunnah?
quiz-385.explanation: The works of the early Sunnah scholars show that Sunnah and Iʿtiqād were not separated.
answers: The Sunnah is preserved, followed, and defended against innovations.
The Sunnah is read only as a historical text.
Bidʿah and Sunnah are treated as equal.
Manhaj plays no role in learning the Dīn.

quiz-386.question: What meaning does the designation Ahl as-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah have?
quiz-386.explanation: The designation joins the Sunnah with the path of the rightly guided community.
answers: Holding fast to the Sunnah and to the rightly guided community.
Holding fast to every new grouping.
Sunnah without Jamāʿah and Jamāʿah without Sunnah.
Religion according to personal taste.

quiz-387.question: What danger exists when someone speaks without knowledge in great religious disputes?
quiz-387.explanation: The Salaf warned against speaking without knowledge, especially in matters of ʿAqīdah, Manhaj, and judgments about people.
answers: He can lead himself and others into misguidance.
He is automatically guided because he speaks boldly.
Ignorance in great topics is better than silence.
The louder someone speaks, the stronger his proof is.

quiz-388.question: Which attitude belongs to the Adab of knowledge when one cannot answer a religious question?
quiz-388.explanation: Admitting ignorance belongs to the Adab of the scholars and protects against false speech about the Dīn.
answers: To say: I do not know.
To answer something so that one does not appear weak.
To invent an answer.
To answer the question with personal feeling.

quiz-389.question: Which order is correct in the Dīn when someone wants to speak about Islamic matters?
quiz-389.explanation: The Salaf placed knowledge before speech and deed, so that the Dīn is not built upon ignorance.
answers: First knowledge, then speech and action.
First speaking, then looking whether there is proof.
First forming an opinion, then adjusting the sources.
First disputing, then learning.

quiz-390.question: Which rule connects Qurʾān 2:286 with the Ḥadīths about commands according to ability?
quiz-390.explanation: Qurʾān and Sunnah together show that obligation and ability are taken into account in Fiqh.
answers: Duties are carried out according to ability, and الله does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
Ability plays no role in Fiqh.
Every difficulty automatically lifts all duties.
The human being himself determines without proof what is a duty.

quiz-391.question: Which general fiqh maxim is supported by the well-known reports about the prohibition of harm?
quiz-391.explanation: The maxim “lā ḍarar wa-lā ḍirār” belongs to the important legal maxims in Fiqh.
answers: No harm and no reciprocal harm.
Harm is allowed when it brings benefit.
The Dīn pays no regard to harm.
One may harm others so long as it does not become public.

quiz-392.question: Why is a good intention alone not enough in worship when the act itself has no basis?
quiz-392.explanation: The Ḥadīth about intentions and the Ḥadīth about rejected innovations together show the two foundations: Ikhlāṣ and Mutābaʿah.
answers: Because a deed in worship must be both sincere and in accordance with the Sunnah.
Because sincerity always permits every form.
Because the Sunnah is only a recommendation without significance.
Because invention in worship is better than transmission.

quiz-393.question: Which right of الله over His servants is mentioned in the Ḥadīth of Muʿādh رضي الله عنه?
quiz-393.explanation: The Ḥadīth sums up the right of الله over His servants in Tawḥīd.
answers: That they worship Him and associate nothing with Him.
That they call upon angels only.
That they worship only when there is need.
That they divide worship between الله and creatures.

quiz-394.question: Which right of the servants is mentioned in the Ḥadīth of Muʿādh رضي الله عنه when they worship الله and associate nothing with Him?
quiz-394.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the immense standing of Tawḥīd and the promise for its people.
answers: That الله does not punish them.
That they become independent of الله.
That they are saved without Tawḥīd.
That they may abandon the duties.

quiz-395.question: What meaning does the Ḥadīth have, that whoever dies without having associated anything with الله enters Paradise?
quiz-395.explanation: The Ḥadīth shows the central place of Tawḥīd and the gravity of Shirk.
answers: Tawḥīd is the greatest foundation of salvation.
Shirk has no significance in Islam.
Every religion leads to Paradise independently of Tawḥīd.
Tawḥīd is only a side topic.

quiz-396.question: Which warning follows from the Ḥadīth that whoever dies while calling upon something besides الله enters the Fire?
quiz-396.explanation: The Ḥadīth warns against Shirk in invocation and shows the importance of pure Tawḥīd.
answers: Calling upon others besides الله is an immense danger.
Duʿāʾ to others besides الله is always harmless.

Because an individual statement does not yet constitute a demonstrated agreement of all qualified scholars.

quiz-644.question: Which classical disagreement exists concerning the marriage contract of an adult woman of sound understanding?
quiz-644.explanation: In Ḥanafī fiqh, an adult woman of sound understanding may in principle conclude a marriage contract herself, while questions such as equality of status and an appropriate bridal gift remain legally relevant. The majority of the other schools regards the Walī as a condition of validity.
answers: The Ḥanafī school in principle allows her to conclude the contract herself under legal conditions; the majority requires a Walī.
All four schools of law declare the Walī without exception to be without significance.
Only the Šāfiʿī school allows her to conclude the contract herself without a Walī.
The Mālikī and Ḥanbalī schools forbid every marriage contract concluded by a Walī.

quiz-645.question: Which well-known disagreement exists concerning lawfully worn gold jewelry that reaches the Niṣāb?
quiz-645.explanation: The Ḥanafī school treats gold and silver in principle as subject to Zakāh even in the form of jewelry. The majority distinguishes in the case of permissible, usual use and in principle does not prescribe Zakāh for this, so long as no further grounds such as trade or excessive hoarding are present.
answers: All four schools of law declare it without exception not subject to Zakāh.
Only the Mālikī school declares all jewelry subject to Zakāh.
The Ḥanafī school in principle requires Zakāh; the majority exempts usual, lawfully used jewelry under its conditions.
Jewelry is subject to Zakāh only if it has never been worn.

quiz-646.question: Which well-known disagreement exists concerning the Qurʾān recitation of a person praying behind the Imām?
quiz-646.explanation: The Ḥanafī school emphasizes the listening and silence of the person praying behind. In the Šāfiʿī school, al-Fātiḥah in principle belongs to the recitation duty of every person praying, including behind the Imām.
answers: The Šāfiʿī school forbids al-Fātiḥah, while the Ḥanafī school requires it in every Rakʿah.
The Ḥanafī school in principle does not have the person praying behind the Imām recite; the Šāfiʿī school in principle requires al-Fātiḥah also from that person.
All schools declare the Imām’s recitation invalid.
The question concerns exclusively voluntary night prayers.

quiz-647.question: What characterizes a report transmitted as muʿallaq?
quiz-647.explanation: In the Muʿallaq, at least one transmitter is missing from the beginning of the chain. The mere inclusion of such a report in a work does not yet automatically determine its final assessment of authenticity.
answers: The text contains an additional explanation by a transmitter.
Two transmitters accidentally exchange their names.
The report is transmitted by a particularly large number of people.
At the beginning of the chain of transmission, one or more consecutive transmitters are omitted.

quiz-648.question: What is a report transmitted as muʿḍal?
quiz-648.explanation: The Muʿḍal has a particularly severe form of interruption in the chain, because two or more consecutive transmitters have been omitted.
answers: A report in whose chain of transmission at least two consecutive transmitters are missing.
A report whose text consists exclusively of two sentences.
A report that two Ṣaḥābah transmit jointly.
A report with two fully preserved chains of transmission.

quiz-649.question: What does Idrāǧ in a Ḥadīth designate?
quiz-649.explanation: A Mudraǧ can arise when a transmitter’s explanation is mistakenly understood as part of the original Ḥadīth text, or when material appears to have been inserted into the chain.
answers: Transmission through a particularly high-ranking Isnād.
Shortening a report without changing its meaning.
Inserting words or information into the Isnād or Matn that originally did not belong to that part of the prophetic report.
Transmitting a Ḥadīth in several languages.

quiz-650.question: What characterizes a report transmitted as maqlūb?
quiz-650.explanation: In the Maqlūb, for example, the names of two transmitters may be exchanged, a chain assigned to another text, or parts of the wording rearranged.
answers: The report has exclusively a very short chain of transmission.
Names, attributions, or wordings are exchanged or reversed.
The report is transmitted exclusively according to the meaning.
The report contains a legal disagreement.

ikhlas-question-1.question: What matters in Ikhlāṣ?
ikhlas-question-1.explanation: Ikhlāṣ means performing the deed sincerely for Allah.
answers: The quantity of visible good deeds
Performing a deed for Allah alone
Receiving people’s recognition

ikhlas-question-2.question: An action is well intended, but it contradicts the Sunnah. What is missing?
ikhlas-question-2.explanation: Sincere intention must be joined by conformity with the Sunnah.
answers: Outward correctness according to the Sunnah
More praise from others
The intention of being seen

ikhlas-question-3.question: You help someone without others finding out. What is decisive?
ikhlas-question-3.explanation: The example joins directing oneself to Allah with a correct action.
answers: That the deed later becomes publicly known
That you receive praise for it
That you act for Allah and the help is lawful

ikhlas-question-4.question: What do you examine before a good deed?
ikhlas-question-4.explanation: Al-Fuḍayl names the two foundations: sincere and correct.
answers: Whether others will be impressed
Whether the intention is for Allah and the deed conforms to the Sunnah
Whether the action is as conspicuous as possible

selbstpruefung-question-1.question: Whom does the believer examine according to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī?
selbstpruefung-question-1.explanation: The Athar mentions the believer’s self-examination for the sake of Allāh.
answers: First himself and his actions
Exclusively other people
Only his financial situation

selbstpruefung-question-2.question: For whom, according to this statement, will the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection be easier?
selbstpruefung-question-2.explanation: Al-Ḥasan links the easing of the reckoning with self-examination in this world.
answers: For those who completely forget their own accountability
For those who already call themselves to account in this world
For those who exalt themselves over others

selbstpruefung-question-3.question: Why does the reckoning become heavy for some people?
selbstpruefung-question-3.explanation: The report sets action without accountability over against conscious self-examination.
answers: Because in this world they let their conduct run on without self-examination
Because they regularly corrected their faults
Because they felt responsible before Allah

selbstpruefung-question-4.question: How does the more detailed Athar describe conduct toward an enticing desire?
selbstpruefung-question-4.explanation: The longer wording mentions refraining from something desired and returning to self-examination after a lapse.
answers: Fulfill it without fail whenever one desires it
Free oneself from every regard for one’s own conduct
Examine one’s own desire and leave it when it is not right

tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-1.question: According to the transmitted explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās, what is joined with justice?
tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-1.explanation: Ibn ʿAbbās is credited with explaining justice by the testimony of faith.
answers: The testimony of faith that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah
Only social prosperity
A particular journey

tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-2.question: How is Iḥsān rendered in the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās treated here?
tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-2.explanation: The meaning rendered here stresses the fulfillment of the duties.
answers: As the omission of all duties
As the fulfillment of the duties
As outward wealth

tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-3.question: What does the transmitted statement of Qatādah emphasize?
tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-3.explanation: Qatādah mentions the good character traits and the prohibition of bad actions.
answers: That good character is meaningless
That only speech is decisive
That good character traits are commanded and bad ones are forbidden

tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-4.question: How are these German statements marked on the source card?
tawhid-iman-akhlaq-question-4.explanation: They are rendered as sense-faithful Athār, not as prophetic Ḥadīṯs.
answers: As sense-faithful renderings of early reports
As verbatim prophetic Ḥadīṯs
As entirely newly invented legal rulings

wissen-adab-question-1.question: Which two areas are placed side by side in Ibn Sīrīn’s statement as objects of learning?
wissen-adab-question-1.explanation: Ibn Sīrīn emphasizes that good conduct of life was learned with the same seriousness as knowledge.
answers: Knowledge and public oratory
Knowledge and exemplary conduct of life
Knowledge and the number of students

wissen-adab-question-2.question: What does al-hady mean in the context of this report?
wissen-adab-question-2.explanation: Al-hady here denotes good guidance and conduct; acquiring knowledge and lived adab belong together.
answers: The exact order of lesson topics
The quantity of texts learned by heart
Exemplary conduct of life and good behavior

wissen-adab-question-3.question: Which form of learning does the mentioned observation of al-Qāsim illustrate?
wissen-adab-question-3.explanation: Observing the conduct of life and behavior of an example shows that adab was also learned through lived examples.
answers: Learning from a lived example
The evaluation of public speeches
The checking of written records

wissen-adab-question-4.question: Which course of action best puts Ibn Sīrīn’s basic idea into practice in dealing with others?
wissen-adab-question-4.explanation: Careful acquisition of knowledge and good conduct are taken seriously together; the one does not replace the other.
answers: Citing as many proofs as possible without regard to tone
Learning knowledge carefully and treating people respectfully
Putting courtesy in the place of attested knowledge

qQuotes.Lernt, lernt! Wenn ihr dann Wissen erlan: Learn, learn! Then, when you have acquired knowledge, act upon it.
qQuotes.Die Allah liebsten Taten sind diejenigen: The deeds most beloved to Allah are those that are most constant, even if they are small.
qQuotes.Halte dich an die Überlieferungen derer,: Hold to the reports of those who were before you, even if people reject you; and beware of the opinions of people, even if they adorn them for you with fine words.
qQuotes.Der letzte Teil dieser Ummah wird nicht: The latter part of this Ummah will not be set right except by that through which its first part was set right.
qQuotes.Wenn eine Tat aufrichtig ist, aber nicht: If a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it is not accepted, until it is sincere and correct. Sincere is when it is for Allah; and correct is when it is in accordance with the Sunnah.
qQuotes.Wenn ihr in meinem Buch etwas findet, da: If you find in my book something that contradicts the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then take the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and leave my statement.
qQuotes.Wer behauptet, dass der Allerbarmer sich: Whoever claims that the Most Merciful has risen over the Throne, contrary to what has become firmly established in the hearts of the general body of the Muslims, is a Jahmī.
qQuotes.Ich glaube an einen Herrn, der tut, was: I believe in a Lord who does what He wills.
qQuotes.Wenn ein Jahmī zu dir sagt: Ich glaube n: If a Jahmī says to you: I do not believe in a Lord who descends from His place / moves, then you say: I believe in a Lord who does what He wills.
qQuotes.Er ist an Seinem makān und nähert sich S: He is in His makān and draws near to His creation as He wills.
qQuotes.Dies haben die Salaf nicht getan … Wäre: The Salaf did not do this … Had it been pure good or predominantly good, the Salaf would have had a greater right to it than we do.
qQuotes.Ich habe mit niemandem diskutiert, außer: I have not debated with anyone except that I wished the truth would appear through his tongue or through my tongue.
qQuotes.Hochmut ist, die Wahrheit abzulehnen und: Arrogance is to reject the truth and to deem people of little worth.
qQuotes.Dass ein Mann sein Recht von dem nimmt,: That a man takes his right from the one who withholds it from him.
qQuotes.Wisse also, dass es keinen anbetungswürd: Know, then, that there is no god worthy of worship except الله.
qQuotes.Wer liebt, dass die Männer für ihn stehe: Whoever likes that men stand for him, let him take his place in the Fire.
qQuotes.Aus Ḫurāsān kam niemals jemand hervor, d: From Ḫurāsān there never came forth anyone who had memorized more Ḥadīṯ than Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, and no one came from there to ʿIrāq who was more knowledgeable than he.
qQuotes.Lernt den Islam … haltet euch an den ger: Learn Islam … hold to the straight path … and beware of these desires.
qQuotes.Wer mit seinem Ohr einem Anhänger der Bi: Whoever listens with his ear to a follower of Bidʿah, protection is withdrawn from him and he is left to himself.
qQuotes.Nichts ist seltener als zwei Dinge: ein: Nothing is rarer than two things: a pure dirham and a man who acts according to the Sunnah.
qQuotes.Du bist nur jemand, der Genuss sucht: du: You are only someone seeking enjoyment: you listen and dictate. From knowledge, only action is wanted.
qQuotes.Dass ich die Nacht schlafend verbringe u: That I spend the night asleep and repent in the morning is dearer to me than that I spend the night standing in prayer and be self-satisfied in the morning.
qQuotes.Wenn Allah für einen Diener Gutes will,: When Allah wills good for a servant, He opens for him the door to action and closes for him the door of disputation.
qQuotes.Die Muslime sind sich einig, dass wer Al: The Muslims agree that whoever reviles Allah, or reviles His Messenger ﷺ, or rejects anything of what Allah has sent down, or kills a prophet among the prophets of Allah, is thereby a Kafir, even if he affirms everything that Allah has sent down.
qQuotes.Steh dort, wo die Leute standen, und sag: Stand where the people stood, and say what they said, and be silent about that on which they were silent. For they stood on the basis of knowledge, and they held back on the basis of clear insight.
qQuotes.Die Mehrheit der Menschen hat die Jamāʿa: Most people have left the Jamāʿah. The Jamāʿah is that which conforms to the truth, even if you are alone.
qQuotes.Der Anhänger einer Bidʿah nimmt nicht an: The follower of a Bidʿah does not increase in exertion except that he thereby only increases further in distance from Allah.
qQuotes.Bei Allah, o Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, wir wol: By Allah, O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, we only wanted the good.
qQuotes.Wer mit einem Anhänger der Bidʿah sitzt,: Whoever sits with a follower of Bidʿah does not remain free of one of three things: either he becomes a Fitnah for others, or something falls into his heart by which he stumbles and Allah thereby causes him to enter the Fire, or he says: By Allah, I do not care what they say, I am sure of myself. But whoever feels secure from Allah regarding his Dīn even for a moment, He will snatch it from him.
qQuotes.Es werden Leute erscheinen, die den Qurʾ: People will appear who recite the Qurʾān, yet it does not go beyond their throats. They leave the Dīn as the arrow passes through the game.
qQuotes.Der Muʾmin vereint Iḥsān und Furcht ; de: The Muʾmin combines Iḥsān and fear; the Munāfiq combines an evil deed and a feeling of security.
qQuotes.Wer Allah Seiner Schöpfung ähnlich macht: Whoever likens Allah to His creation has committed Kufr. And whoever denies that with which Allah has described Himself has committed Kufr. And that with which Allah has described Himself and with which His Messenger ﷺ has described Him is not Tašbīh.
qQuotes.Ich nehme dich aus dieser Welt; nicht du: I take you out of this world; not by death.
qQuotes.Die Mehrheit der Salaf und der Muslime v: The majority of the Salaf and of the Muslims held that it took place with the body and in a waking state.
qQuotes.Mit nichts hatte ich schwerer zu kämpfen: I have not struggled with anything more severely than with my intention, for it keeps changing with me.
qQuotes.Taqwā gegenüber Allah besteht nicht dari: Taqwā toward Allah does not consist in fasting by day and praying by night while committing wrongs in between. Rather, Taqwā consists in leaving what Allah has forbidden and in fulfilling what Allah has made obligatory. Whoever is granted further good beyond that, for him it is good that is added to further good.
qQuotes.Er soll das Geld zuerst zurückgeben. Den: He should return the money first. For his Dhikr will not be accepted until he has returned it.
qQuotes.Das bedeutet: Sie rufen Ihn mit Tawḥīd u: This means: they call upon Him with Tawḥīd and with sincerity toward Him, and they worship Him.
They should forgive and show forbearance. Do you not love that Allah forgive you? And Allah is All-Forgiving, Merciful.
qQuotes.Eine Ameise biss einen der früheren Prop: An ant bit one of the earlier prophets. Thereupon he had an entire ant colony burned. Then Allah revealed to him: Only because an ant bit you, have you destroyed an entire people that glorifies Allah?
qQuotes.Man schützt seine Familie, indem man sie: One protects one’s family by calling them to obedience to Allah, holding them back from disobedience, and helping them to fulfill Allah’s commands.
qQuotes.Rechtschaffenheit ist guter Charakter. U: Righteousness is good character. And sin is that which stirs unease in your Nafs and which you do not want people to know about.
qQuotes.Schmückt das Wissen durch euch selbst –: Adorn knowledge through yourselves, and do not adorn yourselves with knowledge.
qQuotes.Sie lernten die vorbildliche Lebensführu: They learned exemplary conduct just as they learned knowledge.
qQuotes.Tawḥīd ist das Fundament; Īmān verlangt: Tawḥīd is the foundation; īmān requires obedience, and character shows itself in action.
qQuotes.Der Gläubige wacht über sich selbst und: The believer watches over himself and calls himself to account for Allāh’s sake. The reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be easier for those who have already called themselves to account in this world. The reckoning will be hard, however, for those who have conducted their affairs without calling themselves to account.
